item.title: Fantasy Football: Jaylen Waddle finally shows up, Bears' backfield goes off and more bold predictions for Week 11
item.description: Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold call for fantasy football in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
There aren't many weeks left in the fantasy football regular season; you can't hold anything back. That means you need to be bold to come out on top. Our Yahoo analysts share their one bold prediction for fantasy football in Week 11.

Jaylen Waddle turns in second WR1 finish of '26

I realize that trusting any WR tied to Bo Nix is like playing with fire. But there have been some fantasy-related improvements to Denver's passing game. First, Nix is throwing more relative to expectations. He's been at a +3.0% PROE over the last month, a 180-degree flip from Weeks 1-4 (-2.5%). He's also throwing to the middle of the field, where passing efficiency jumps, at the sixth-highest rate. And he's fifth in EPA per dropback on those throws.

That's where Jaylen Waddle comes into play. He's led the Broncos in targets on concepts over the MoF (2.49 YPRR). That's where the Raiders have been consistently beaten on defense. Opposing WRs are averaging 87.6 YPG and a smooth 24.8 PPR PPG on those throws alone. While both were on broken plays, both Seahawks' WRs found themselves in the end zone with the ball on throws between the numbers. Assuming Waddle clears protocol, he'll give us his second WR1 performance of the season in Week 11. — Chris Allen

Swift, Monangai both finish as top-12 fantasy RBs

The Bears' backfield will finally be at full strength in Week 11 with Kyle Monangai returning after a five-game absence due to a toe injury. He's picked the right defense to get back on the field against, since the Saints are allowing the second-most fantasy points to RBs, the eighth-most rushing yards and the fourth-most rushing touchdowns. Chicago also has an implied total of 30 points, so we can project a lot of scoring from Ben Johnson's crew.

New Orleans has let 11 different backs reach double-digit fantasy points, including three sets of teammates. One of those duos was Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson Jr., who both finished as top-12 fantasy RBs in Week 4. Monangai and D'Andre Swift also accomplished that feat in the opener versus the Panthers, which was one of the four games they've shared the field together this season. Get ready for them to do it again, now that the bar is lower with six teams on bye. — Justin Boone

Chig Okonkwo finishes as a top-5 fantasy TE

Over the last month, Chig Okonkwo has the seventh-best TE volume and a top-5 route share when accounting for his Week 10 injury. He still has the big-play ability he's had throughout his career and can turn his volume into better production against a Bengals defense ranking bottom-5 versus TEs. Cincinnati is forcing opposing offenses into going pass-heavy, is able to slow down receivers on the outside, but has still allowed the second-most yards on the fourth-most targets to TEs inside, without playing against any of the top fantasy tight ends. If Okonkwo has the ball in his hands that much, he's bound to make some big plays after the catch. — Joel Smyth

Cam Ward finishes as a top-10 fantasy QB against Dallas

I know Cam Ward's name hasn't exactly been synonymous with fantasy scoring, but he's quietly put together two pretty damn good games. Dallas, meanwhile, has been loudly awful on defense for more than two seasons. New defensive play-caller this week? Cool. I'm still calling a top-10 finish for Ward. He's thrown for 535 yards and four touchdowns over his last two games and added another 80 yards on the ground. Dallas is giving up 7.8 yards per pass attempt and has already allowed 19 passing touchdowns. Brock Purdy just hung 389 yards and three scores on them in 28 attempts. Ward doesn't have to do all that. Give me 250 through the air, two touchdown passes and another 35 on the ground. And if Dak Prescott gets Dallas out to an early lead, good. That's more chances for Ward to throw against a defense I'm still going out of my way to attack. — Ray Garvin

Tony Pollard has six catches or 80 yards receiving (or both)

The Titans normally don't throw the ball much to Pollard, but that's changed in the last three games — the underrated back has collected 14 catches in that span. And the Dallas defense is especially terrible when it comes to tracking running backs in the passing game — Christian McCaffrey had a field day against this unit last week. Tennessee's offense has been up to code in the last three weeks, and this game features a 54.5-point total. Pollard is going to crush in his revenge game against the Cowboys, and part of the story will be written through the air. — Scott Pianowski

Christian McCaffrey catches double-digit passes

On the surface, maybe this doesn’t sound bold but funny enough, McCaffrey has done this just once in over 60 regular and postseason games with the 49ers. It happened last season when he caught 10 passes against the Cardinals in a low-scoring game. The 49ers lead the league in getting five players out in the route, accounting for 75% of their dropbacks. That’s unlikely to change against Minnesota and its blitz looks. I expect McCaffrey to be heavily involved as a receiver in the flats, as an escort screen option and on extended checkdowns. There will be voids in coverage against Minnesota there and Brock Purdy has been excellent at picking the right spots to attack. — Matt Harmon

item.title: NFL news, live updates: Puka Nacua might be out for season after MCL surgery; Marlon Humphrey sent home from Ravens' facility, won't play in Week 11
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news heading into Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
We are officially halfway done with the 2026 NFL season.

The NFL heads into Week 11, highlighted by the year's final international game: the Minnesota Vikings take on the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Mexico, for "Sunday Night Football."

Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua might be done for the year after undergoing surgery on his MCL on Tuesday. Nacua was already on injured reserve with multiple injuries, but head coach Sean McVay says that he is now poised to miss “a couple months.”

That news came one day after Nacua was reportedly suspended three games by the NFL for violating the league's personal conduct policy, as a result of the receiver's series of incidents this offseason; Nacua is serving the suspension while on IR.

The Detroit Lions will be without Aidan Hutchinson, who suffered a torn ACL during last week's win over the New England Patriots. New England will be without quarterback Drake Maye for the foreseeable future due to an ankle injury, though the extent of it — including how much time he will miss — has not been specified.

Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said that Joe Milton III will once again be under center as the team looks to shake its seven-game losing streak. Meanwhile, the Baltimore Ravens sent home Marlon Humphrey, ruling him inactive for this weekend as part of the fallout from his comments about "criminals" in Baltimore.

Another injury to watch this week is Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield, who was spotted in a walking boot during the team's bye last week and could miss this week. This would pave the way for undrafted rookie QB Jalon Daniels to be back under center against the Lions.

item.title: NFL predictions: Titans-Cowboys matchup will be a shootout
item.description: This should be an entertaining game to watch!
item.content:encoded:
For the first time in years, fantasy football people are touting a Tennessee Titans quarterback. Cam Ward has been playing better over the last month, and the Titans are facing a Dallas Cowboys pass defense that has gotten lit up in recent weeks. The stars are aligned for a big game from Ward. That probably means we are in for a letdown.

We are all very familiar with the struggles the Titans’ pass defense has. They cannot get pressure on the quarterback with Jeffery Simmons gone, and they cannot cover anyone on the back end. Dak Prescott and the Cowboys’ offense should move the ball down the field at will.

The total for this game opened at 53.5 at FanDuel Sportsbook. It currently sits at 54.5. It is the highest total on the board for Week 11. I’m not sure the Titans have ever been in a game that featured the highest total for a week.

This game sets up to look a lot like the Cincinnati Bengals game from a few weeks ago. The Titans lost that one 43-36 in overtime. Joe Burrow threw for 462 yards and 5 touchdowns. Ward threw for 304 yards and 2 touchdowns.

To me, having an entertaining game to watch where Ward plays well but the Titans ultimately lose is a win, win, win scenario. That is probably what will happen here, but I have a feeling the Titans are going to pull off an upset….

item.title: Here’s how the Raiders can still make the postseason in the AFC
item.description: Las Vegas still can make a playoff run
item.content:encoded:
The Houston Texans won on Thursday night, dropping the Las Vegas Raiders to the No. 10 spot in the AFC playoff picture as they prepare to play at the Denver Broncos on Sunday in Week 11.

Let’s break down the current AFC standings and check out some paths to the postseason.

AFC playoff standings with Texans win on Thursday Night Football

1. Buffalo Bills (8-1)

2. Kansas City Chiefs (7-2, 3-1 AFCW, 6-1 AFC)

3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2, 6-2 AFC, win over CIN)

4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2, 5-2 AFC, loss to JAX)

5. Denver Broncos (7-2, 2-1 AFCW)

6. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3)

7. Cleveland Browns (6-4)

8. New England Patriots (5-5)

9. Houston Texans (4-6, 4-4 AFC, SOV tiebreaker over LV)

10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6, 3-3 AFC)

11. Baltimore Ravens (4-6, 2-5 AFC)

12. Indianapolis Colts (3-7)

13. New York Jets (2-8)

14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .400 SOV)

15. Miami Dolphins (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .200 SOV)

16. Tennessee Titans (1-8, 1-6 AFC)

Explaining the 4-6 tiebreaker

The Texans, Raiders, and Ravens go into a three-way tiebreaker where the Ravens are eliminated on AFC record. The Texans and Raiders are both .500 in that tiebreaker so it goes to Strength of Victory. The Texans’ wins came against teams with a combined 12 wins while the Raiders wins were against teams with a combined 7 wins. The Texans slip in front for now as the 9 seed. 

The Ravens and Raiders go into another tiebreaker with the Ravens’ 3-3 record in the AFC beating Baltimore’s 2-5 conference record. The Raiders are 10th. 

Explaining the 7-2 tiebreaker

The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. 

The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beaten both of the others, so it moves to the AFC record tiebreaker. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed for now. 

Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. 

The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card.

item.title: What will make the 2026 Eagles season a successful one following the bye week?
item.description: Believe it or not, the Eagles can still find success in a lost season.
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season won’t be resulting in a Super Bowl championship. The playoff streak is also likely ending at five seasons.

This season is a lost cause in terms of expectations from the summer. That doesn’t mean the 2026 season can’t be deemed a success.

Bear with me here.

Since the Eagles are 2-7 and aren’t expected to make the playoffs this year, there are some factors remaining in this season that can carry over into 2027. The wins and losses aren’t as important (well maybe the losses), but some aspects from 2026 can play into how the 2027 Eagles shape out.

So what can make the remainder of this Eagles season a success? There are a few things to hope for in this lost season.

1. Finding the No. 2 QB

One of the biggest developments heading into the season was the Eagles’ handling of the backup quarterback. They didn’t have a backup quarterback, so they used the “competitive advantage” charade between Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee up until the Week 1 inactives were posted.

Dalton isn’t with the Eagles anymore and McKee was benched after three subpar starts. The backup quarterback “competition,” played out to the Eagles’ biggest fear.

Joe Milton is making his second start on Sunday and Cole Payton is waiting in the wings for his opportunity once he’s ready to play. The Eagles need to hope one of the two can play well enough to be Jalen Hurts’ backup in 2027 — assuming Hurts is able to play football again.

The perfect scenario for the Eagles? Milton plays fine the remainder of the season, or good enough to keep around.

2. A top-5 draft pick

Easy one right? Losing more games actually helps the Eagles in a lost season.

The Eagles still have talent and core players on this roster that will contribute in 2027, but this season has been a disaster with all the injuries, the subpar offensive line (with trades and retirements), and discombobulation on offense.

The Eagles have eight games remaining in this season. as the .504 opponents win percentage is the rest of the season is 14th-hardest in the NFL. They likely won’t lose out, but a 4-13 record could wrap up a top-5 draft pick.

The Eagles currently have the No. 5 pick in the draft, per Tankathon. They’re currently in position to get that top-5 pick.

3. Continued growth of Makai Lemon

Lemon has finally acclimated to the NFL after missing the majority of the spring and summer with a hamstring injury. Even though the Eagles were banking on Lemon to be an instant impact player in the offense, a slow start for the rookie was expected.

Over the last three games, Lemon has 20 catches for 185 yards and a touchdown. The 9.3 yards per catch isn’t great, but Lemon was the WR1 in a depleted offense with the QB3 from Week 1 and a quarterback signed a month ago.

With Devonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back, the Eagles should see more production from Lemon in the slot. He won’t be the primary option in the offense, but Lemon can be a more efficient pass catcher as the WR3 — which is expected to be his role in 2027.

Lemon has shown he can play in the NFL. The next step is to catch passes consistently and for the Eagles to expand his route tree. One of the two should come to fruition in the final eight games.

4. Markel Bell’s development at right tackle

Bell might be the worst offensive tackle in the league. He wasn’t supposed to play significant snaps this season, as this year was supposed to be the final one for Lane Johnson. Turns out it was, but Johnson retired after four games and didn’t finish out the year.

Bell wasn’t ready, and it’s shown in pass protection. He’s allowed five sacks, 18 pressures, and has been beaten by a defender 25 times in 253 pass-blocking snaps — a beat rate of 9.9%. Only the Green Bay Packers’ Anthony Belton has a higher beat rate amongst offensive linemen with 100+ pass-blocking snaps.

The Eagles have to see improvement out of Bell in the final eight games to determine if he’s worth building around at right tackle. If Bell doesn’t improve, a new offensive line coach may be coming (Chris Kuper may likely be gone anyway) and the Eagles will have to seriously consider selecting a tackle with that top-10 pick in the NFL Draft.

If Bell can improve and become a competant right tackle in the final eight games, that’s a significant win for the Eagles in 2027.

5. Dontayvion Wicks showing he can be a WR2

The early returns for Wicks as a WR2 have been positive, but an ankle injury has hurt Wicks’ progress in what was looking to be a promising year. Wicks has been productive in his six games, having 19 catches for 284 yards and a touchdown — 14.9 yards per catch. He was on pace for 805 receiving yards prior to the injury.

While Wicks has been a deep-ball receiver, most of that productivity came when Jalen Hurts was the quarterback. Wicks has only played one game post-Hurts, having two catches for 24 yards before missing the past three games with that ankle injury.

With Joe Milton at quarterback, there should be opportunities for Wicks to be a deep-ball threat — even with the offensive line struggling in pass protection. Wicks should open up the offense, as he has 25 games (this year and next) to showcase to the Eagles he can be a core player in the offense going forward.

6. Jonathan Greenard becoming an impact player

Like Lemon this summer, Greenard wasn’t going to be in football shape at the start of the season due to the pectoral injury that kept him out of camp. A slow start was expected, but Greenard didn’t get his first sack until Week 8 against the New York Giants.

The Eagles started Greenard on a pitch count, and he’s slowly worked his way to 50% of the snaps (which occurred in the Giants game). The production hasn’t been ideal — even for a part-time player — as Greenard has just a sack, 10 pressures, and an 11.9% pressure rate this season.

Greenard appears to be back in football shape, with the pectoral injury behind him. It’s time to see the player the Eagles are paying $24.5 million a season for, the version of Greenard that had a 16.7% pressure rate over the past two seasons.

Greenard was an elite pass rusher two years ago. Shoulder and pectoral injuries have taken away that elite status.

The Eagles need Greenard to be close to elite if they want to get the pass rush going. Philadelphia is 27th in the NFL in pressure rate (32.3%) and 28th in sack rate (5.1%).

Greenard returning to a Pro Bowl level would increase those numbers.

7. Jihaad Campbell showing why he was a first-round pick

Campbell was handed the keys to a starting job at off-ball linebacker this summer, and is the reason why the Eagles moved on from Nakobe Dean. Philadelphia couldn’t pay everyone, and Dean was a casualty of having to pay other premium players.

This is why the Eagles drafted Campbell two years ago, preparing for the inevitability they were going to lose Dean. Campbell was solid in his rookie season as a linebacker and pass rusher, but is strictly an off-ball linebacker this season.

Poor performance and injuries have led to Jeremiah Trotter Jr. outperforming Campbell, but the Eagles are giving the first-round pick a long leash (as expected). Campbell has to improve in coverage, as he’s allowed 73.1% of passes thrown his way as the primary defender to be caught, with opposing quarterbacks having a 112.7 passer rating targeting him.

This is on Campbell to get himself in position and improve in coverage, or else he’ll be playing for his job in 2027.

8. Jalyx Hunt living up to the training camp hype

Hunt was arguably the best defensive player in training camp. That production — against the Eagles offensive line — hasn’t come close to translating in the regular season.

Hunt doesn’t have a sack through eight games, and has only 16 pressures and a 10.5% pressure rate. He also has just six quarterback hits as well, no where close to the pass rusher that had 5.5 sacks, 16 quarterback hits, two interceptions, a forced fumble, and a 16.8% pressure rate from Weeks 10-17 last season (which were the weeks Jaelan Phillips played).

Those numbers were expected to be identical with Jonathan Greenard around — pairing Hunt with another No.1 pass rusher. Hunt hasn’t come close to that production due to Greenard’s pectoral injury and knee and ankle injuries suffered in Week 5.

The Eagles pass rush hasn’t clicked with Greenard and Hunt struggling. Hunt may also be playing for a contract, as Nolan Smith has been the more productive pass rusher this year. The Eagles need Hunt to turn his season around if he’s going to be a core player going forward.

Perhaps a sack will get him going.

Another week without Kenneth Walker III? It's looking that way for the Kansas City Chiefs.

After missing Week 10 due to groin tightness, the Chiefs running back has yet to practice this week and is in jeopardy of missing Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals. Should he not be able to go, rookie Emmett Johnson, who rushed for 101 yards and caught two receiving touchdowns last week, will once again take on the starter's role.

"It's getting better, but with those, you don't wanna do something stupid, right?" Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said of Walker. "Put him out there, and it's still bugging him a little bit, but he's feeling a lot better than he was. We'll just see. I mean, it's a day-to-day thing, so we'll just see how it goes."

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent surgery to repair his MCL this week, head coach Sean McVay announced on Friday. The procedure will rule him out for the next few months, which could result in him missing the rest of the 2026 NFL season.

"We always thought [it] was a possibility," McVay said regarding Nacua's surgery. "It's going to be a couple months and we're going to have to go on without him."

The 6-4 Rams, who are on a bye in Week 11 and play Thanksgiving Eve against the Green Bay Packers, are currently tied for second in the NFC West and have seven more games left in the regular season. McVay did not have a definitive timeline for a return. The team is currently scheduled to play its Week 18 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Jan. 3, a game that could be flexed depending on what the playoff picture looks like at the time.

McVay did not rule out a Nacua return should the Rams make the postseason, but said, "you're planning on not having him."

Other Week 11 injuries to monitor:

  • Luther Burden III (concussion) has cleared protocol after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit in Week 8 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The Chicago Bears wide receiver logged back-to-back full practices on Wednesday and Thursday, a good indication he'll be available against the New Orleans Saints. Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons isn't concerned about a knee issue that kept him limited this week. "Like 99 problems, but this ain't one," he said.

  • Injuries that kept him limited in Wednesday's practice did not keep Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (ankle/quad) away from being on the field Thursday. The Raiders' leading receiver exited Sunday's loss to the Seattle Seahawks after just 11 snaps with an ankle issue.

  • DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has missed the past three games for the Philadelphia Eagles, but says he's 100% and has felt that way for a while. Smith said he was able to play last week against the Carolina Panthers, but some things are out of his control. "I didn't bust my ass this whole summer, I didn't continue to get up at 4:30 in the morning every day, to come out here and not play," he said. "My focus has been to getting where I was supposed to be."

item.title: Rams hope to have Kobie Turner back for Week 12
item.description: Rams head coach Sean McVay shared a negative update on wide receiver Puka Nacua's health on Friday, but he had better news regarding defensive tackle Kobie Turner.
item.content:encoded:
Rams head coach Sean McVay shared a negative update on wide receiver Puka Nacua's health on Friday, but he had better news regarding defensive tackle Kobie Turner.

McVay said that the team is planning to activate defensive tackle Kobie Turner from injured reserve ahead of next Wednesday's game against the Packers. Turner has missed the last four games with a groin injury.

Turner had 22 tackles in six games before his injury.

Getting Turner back would give the Rams the full defensive front they envisioned when they traded for Myles Garrett and coaxed Aaron Donald out of retirement this offseason. With Nacua expected to miss the rest of the season and Davante Adams still out, they'll be banking on that defensive front being a major asset to their playoff push.

item.title: Jets confirm Geno Smith’s status for Chargers game after brutal hits
item.description: Cade Klubnik will have to wait to make his first career start.
item.content:encoded:
Cade Klubnik will have to wait to make his first career start.

After being limited in Thursday’s practice, Geno Smith was scheduled to be a full participant on Friday, putting him on track to start Sunday’s game in Los Angeles against the Chargers, according to head coach Aaron Glenn.

“He looks solid,” Glenn said Friday morning. “It’s very encouraging.”

Smith, who was knocked out of last weekend’s loss to the Bills in the third quarter, said earlier this week that he planned on suiting up despite walking with a limp from his injured left ankle.

Through 10 games, Smith has thrown for 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns and three interceptions — ranking seventh in quarterback rating among players who have made at least six starts — but he has also taken the third-most sacks in the league (29) and leads an offense that ranks 25th in scoring (19.4 points per game), having failed to score a touchdown in nine straight quarters.

Smith, 36, has missed only four games since becoming a full-time starter again in 2022.

Klubnik, the 23-year-old rookie backup, completed 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards and an interception in his first regular season appearance last week when Smith exited.

item.title: Davante Adams’ anticipated return against Packers hits a snag
item.description: Any hopes of Davante Adams returning to face his former team on Thanksgiving Eve appear to be fading. Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay poured cold water on speculation...
item.content:encoded:
Any hopes of Davante Adams returning to face his former team on Thanksgiving Eve appear to be fading.

Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay poured cold water on speculation that his star wide receiver could return from a hamstring injury for Wednesday night’s primetime showdown against the Green Bay Packers.

“Don’t think he’s ready quite yet,” McVay told reporters Monday morning. “There is a possibility he’ll be ready the game after the Packers.”

That game would be Thursday, December 3 against the Kansas City Chiefs at SoFi Stadium.

Adams ruptured his hamstring against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6 and was placed on injured reserve. He underwent surgery to “clean up” the hamstring and was expected to miss between 6 and 10 weeks.

It’s another tough break for the Rams, who are already without Puka Nacua following knee surgery, leaving Matthew Stafford dangerously thin at wide receiver for one of the biggest games of their season.

item.title: Packers’ upcoming Wednesday game isn’t their only schedule oddity
item.description: The Packers have a long history of games on just about every day of the week.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers are off this Sunday, but they’re spending their bye week getting ready for their first Wednesday football game in almost a century. We’ve already covered their upcoming Wednesday matchup in some detail, but that got me thinking: when’s the last time the Packers played on every day of the week?

If you’ve ever wondered the same, wonder no longer. I’ve got you covered.

Sunday – Last Sunday

This one’s easy! The Packers last played on Sunday less than a week ago. They lost to the Vikings. It wasn’t great. 

Monday – 2025 vs. Eagles

We last saw the Packers on Monday Night Football midway through the 2025 season, and it was one of the uglier games of the year. On a rainy and cold evening at Lambeau Field, the Packers held the Eagles to just 10 points, but managed just seven points of their own in the home loss. The Packers have a Monday night game remaining on their schedule this year. They’re slated to play the Texans on Monday Night Football in Week 17.

Tuesday – Never!

The Packers have never played a Tuesday football game (but you can bet your Cheesehead the NFL will find a way to make it happen in the near future), although Tuesday games are not exactly rare in NFL history. There have been 26 Tuesday games in NFL history (at least according to what Pro Football Reference has on the books) and they were relatively frequent up until 1948 or so. After that, we only saw the return of Tuesday football during the 2020 COVID-19 pandemic, during which a few postponements pushed games out of their normal slots.

Wednesday – 1938 vs. Cardinals

The Packers helped christen the city of Buffalo’s new football stadium by playing one of the first contests in the new facility, taking down the Chicago Cardinals 28-7. Read all about it here!

Thursday – 2026 vs. Panthers

The Packers’ last Thursday night game was less than a month ago, so no great history there. But you may be interested to know how old of a phenomenon Thursday games actually are. The Packers started playing regular non-Thanksgiving Thursday games around 2007, but have been playing on Thursdays dating back to the 1920s, usually connected to Thanksgiving. The earliest non-Thanksgiving Thursday game I could find came in 1950 against the now-defunct New York Yanks football team.

Friday – 2024 vs. Eagles

In addition to playing on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday this year, the Packers also have a Friday game on the schedule. They’ll play the Bears in their Rivalry costumes on Christmas Day, and depending how the game goes, it’ll either be a nice present or a lump of coal. Sportswriters, start crafting those headlines now.

The Packers last played on a Friday in 2024, facing the Eagles in their season-opening game in Brazil, and the terrible playing surface ended up affecting the Packers for the rest of the season, as defensive lineman Kenny Clark dealt with a season-long injury.

Prior to their loss to the Eagles, the Packers had been on a three-game Friday football winning streak. They beat the Boston Patriots in 1948, the New York Bulldogs in 1949, and the Minnesota Vikings on Christmas Even in 2004.

Saturday – 2025 playoffs vs. Bears

Finally, I know it’s a game Packers fans would rather forget, but they last played on Saturday last season, capping off their 2025 campaign with a playoff loss to the Chicago Bears. 

Counting playoffs, the Packers have played exactly fifty games on Saturdays and until recently they’d done pretty well in the non-traditional slot. Unfortunately, they’re in the midst of a five-game losing skid on Saturdays, including two playoff losses to the 49ers.

There’s nothing confirmed yet, but the Packers could play on a Saturday this year even if they don’t end up making the playoffs. The date for their Week 18 game against the Lions has yet to be determined, and could ultimately end up being on a Saturday. If you enjoy the Packers playing at unusual times, you should be rooting for that — if the Lions’ game ends up being on a Saturday, the Packers will have played a game on every day but Tuesday in the 2026 regular season.

The Giants are coming off a very frustrating loss to the Commanders in Week 10, and they’ll face their biggest challenge of the season this Sunday when the 7-2 Jacksonville Jaguars come to town. The Jags come in hot. They are running away with the AFC South and their margin of victory across their last three contests (all wins) is +75. Believe it or not, this is Big Blue’s first game this season against a team with a winning record.

It’s an important game for the G-Men, who will try to keep some cushion atop the NFC East. But it won’t be easy. Jacksonville ranks near the top of the league in both offense and defense in advanced metrics like DVOA and EPA per play, and they’ve got one of the best kickers in the game.

My picks were 1-2 in Week 10 and after a hot stretch, I’ve got a couple of losing weeks in a row. I’m still over .500 for the season, but not by much.

Let’s get to this week’s picks. All lines and odds are from Fanduel, as of Friday, November 20.

The line for the game is Jaguars -5.5, with a game total of 46.5. Light rain is possible during the game.

  1. Jaguars -5.5 (-120). Can the Giants win this game? Absolutely. Can they keep it close? Affirmative. They’re at home, with three extra days of rest, and the Jaguars could be due for a letdown. Still, this line feels low to me. Jacksonville is an AFC powerhouse with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, while New York is trying to piece it together with a young roster and its third quarterback of the season. John Harbaugh’s team is well coached and last week’s late meltdown aside, New York has been very good in close games. This one could stay close for a while, but in the end, I think Jacksonville will pull away and I’m comfortable with them laying this number on the road. The Jaguars have a +125 point differential, which is the best in the NFL.
  2. Jaguars FIRST HALF -3.5 (-110). I’m double-dipping. No team has been better in the first half than Jacksonville, although they’ve been better at home. They average 15.9 points scored in the first half, and 5.6 points allowed. Both figures rank first in the NFL. I’ll ride those trends and happily give the points in the first half.
  3. Malik Nabers OVER 5.5 receptions (-120). Nabers is coming off back-to-back down games, but he still managed five catches in both. Before that, he had 30 catches across three games. The Jaguars defend the run very well, and they also defend tight ends well. I think New York is going to struggle to run the ball on the Jaguars and could be chasing points. Nabers is going to want to atone for his costly fumble last week, and he should be the focal point of the passing game. Take the over. 

Those are the picks for Week 11. I know, I want the Giants to win too, and I’ll be happy if my first half and game picks blow up in my face.

item.title: Rams star Puka Nacua has knee surgery, likely will miss rest of season
item.description: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua likely will miss the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery on his knee, coach Sean McVay says.
item.content:encoded:
Rams receiver Puka Nacua had knee surgery this week and will be out for “a couple months,” coach Sean McVay said Friday.

Nacua suffered knee and toe injuries when he was hit while carrying the ball on a jet sweep on the Rams’ final offensive play in their victory over the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8.

Will Nacua be out for the season?

“You can pretty much say yes,” McVay said during a videoconference with reporters.

Read more:NFL suspends Rams star Puka Nacua for violating its personal-conduct policy

Nacua has been on injured reserve since last week. McVay delivered the news the day after the NFL suspended Nacua three games without pay for violating the league’s personal-conduct policy.

Nacua, 25, is the defendant in a civil lawsuit brought by a woman who alleges he made an antisemitic remark during a New Year’s Eve dinner and later bit her while riding in a vehicle.

“It was something that we always knew was a possibility,” McVay said of the suspension. “They were great in their communication with us. ... It’s an unfortunate thing. It’s a learning [opportunity]. It’s something that obviously happened a while ago, that there’s been a lot of discussion and dialogue behind the scenes.”

The Rams, who have won four games in a row, play the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night at SoFi Stadium.

Defensive lineman Kobie Turner is expected to return from injured reserve, but receiver Davante Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson still need more time, McVay said.

item.title: Puka Nacua won’t play vs. Seahawks after ‘likely’ season-ending surgery
item.description: Nacua’s timeline would effectively rule him out for the rest of the regular season.
item.content:encoded:
After Thursday’s news that Los Angeles Rams star receiver Puka Nacua’s league-imposed 3-game suspension would be served while on injured reserve, it turns out Nacua’s next game will probably be in the 2027 season anyway.

Rams head coach Sean McVay said on Friday that Nacua, who was placed on IR following MCL and PCL sprains (plus turf toe), will undergo what is likely season-ending knee surgery.

Nacua sustained the injury on a very needless 3rd and 11 handoff when trying to run the clock out against the Washington Commanders. Keep in mind that Nacua was already targeted 19 times and caught 14 passes in this game, in addition to taking a handoff earlier in the contest.

The surgery news obviously means that, barring one hell of an overestimation of his recovery timeline, Nacua will not play against the Seattle Seahawks in Weeks 16 or 18, which could be critical matchups as far as making the playoffs. Davante Adams should be back within the next few weeks after rupturing his hamstring, but if he’s not back any time soon then the Rams could go into upcoming games against the Green Bay packers, Kansas City Chiefs, and San Francisco 49ers without their top two receivers, not to mention injuries to offensive linemen Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton.

LA’s dream superteam is steadily falling apart, and there’s no guarantee at this point that the Christmas Day showdown at Lumen Field will even have playoff implications for the Rams at this stage. Their fate may actually come down to their defense and the Myles Garrett/Aaron Donald combo to step up in the face of a likely passing offense dropoff.

item.title: Five Plays: North Carolina Fourth Quarter
item.description: This was the second time that Koen Entringer came off the edge, even though there was motion to his side of the field. This was a deliberate blitz call to sell out to get a sack, and I love it. This is how you force quarterbacks to beat you with their arm and their decision-making. […]
item.content:encoded:
This was the second time that Koen Entringer came off the edge, even though there was motion to his side of the field. This was a deliberate blitz call to sell out to get a sack, and I love it. This is how you force quarterbacks to beat you with their arm and their decision-making. It works on the true freshman here, after it worked against one of the most experienced quarterbacks in the country earlier in the game.

Koen actually does a better job on this blitz with getting flat once he got around the corner. He doesn’t go where the quarterback will be, but instead, he comes down the line for a step or two before he breaks down so that he can react to the scramble. If he keeps going full speed, he’s going to be left grasping for air. If he angles towards his back shoulder, he’s going to risk a broken tackle. He slows down and gets down the line so that he can react to whatever comes his way.

I can’t get enough of Keyjuan Brown running the ball as if he only gets to eat dinner if he breaks every tackle on the play. He runs through two guys at the point of attack, spins off his own blocker, then he takes Derek McDonald for a ride six yards down the field.

This is also another well-blocked play by the offensive line. I’ve been very critical of these guys, but they were really good last weekend. The name of the game is “a hat on a hat,” and these guys were very good at meeting that standard. They owned their assignments, which gave Keyjuan a lot of opportunities to get nice gains to move the ball down the field. This was my favorite play, but he had a handful of runs where he picked up 8-10 yards with good space to run.

Lincoln Kienholz had some rough moments in this game, and this was the worst one, in my opinion. With the score and the time in this game, they needed him to get this first down, and I think he just had a genuine moment of uncertainty here. He has the space and angle to get a first down if he commits to running this ball off the read action. Instead, he ends up allowing the safety to split the difference on his option to run or pass. That can’t happen with one defender. You force him to commit to one or the other. Kienholz ends up running backwards to make this throw, and then he delivers a poor pass. A really rough moment for him.

I was happy to hear him being hard on himself after the game. It was also good to hear Jeff Brohm look at that as a positive. He’ll turn that negative into a driving force to play better going forward.

This is outstanding effort from Tyler Thompson. He explodes off the ball into a bull rush before he loses his footing. He then crawls on the ground to get the sack. No real analysis here. This is just awesome to see.

This was pointed out on the broadcast, but I’ll do the same here. I have no clue what Stanquan Clark is doing on this play. He is right over the center to start the play, and he just doesn’t really do anything. He takes a few steps back at the snap, and then he just stands still.

I get very excited when this team’s best players make the big plays, like we saw Clark make on Saturday. They need the top guys to play to their potential. I tend to get equally frustrated when they have moments like this. It’s third and short, and a stop would set up a tough decision to kick the field goal or go for it. Imagine if they could have gotten a stop here late in the game. Instead, Clark is right in the middle of the field on a walk-in touchdown.

The point of this series is to analyse and break down plays, but sometimes it’s just nice to marvel at a really good play. Lawayne McCoy makes one of the more underrated plays of the game here by breaking this tackle to get a first down. The Cards needed to run the clock on this drive, and his subtle setup to make this cornerback lean the wrong way on his tackle attempt was so savvy.

Mark Ivey mixed up his pressure looks throughout this game, with safeties coming off the edge with zone behind it, linebackers doing the same with man coverage, and plays like this where Clark comes from depth with a shell zone behind it. They were able to get quick pressure all night long, and you can clearly see how that ups the difficulty level for the quarterback on this play.

Tyler Burgess had looked very good for a true freshman thrust into his first game action, but he can’t even get his eyes up to look for a receiver. My view on pass defense is pretty simple. You either cover well enough to force the quarterback to hold the ball and progress through his reads, or you get there quickly enough that they can’t make their reads. We see the latter here.

I’ve watched an absurd amount of football in my lifetime, and I’ve never seen a game end like this. Especially because if Jordan Shipp possesses this ball for even a split second, it’s a huge first down that could lead to a game-winning field goal. Instead, it’s a big play for Jabari Mack with a very smart decision to go down to seal the game.

item.title: Puka Nacua undergoes MCL surgery, season in jeopardy
item.description: Sean McVay told the media on Friday that Puka Nacua had surgery on his MCL and is out for the next few months
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams have suffered another devastating injury blow, and this one could keep their biggest offensive weapon off the field for the remainder of the 2026 season. On Friday morning, breaking news revealed that wide receiver Puka Nacua underwent surgery to repair his MCL, putting his availability for the rest of the year in serious jeopardy.

Head coach Sean McVay revealed to reporters that Nacua underwent the procedure on Tuesday and is expected to miss a couple of months. With the regular season already moving toward its final stretch, there is a legitimate possibility that Nacua will not play another snap in 2026.

The injury originally occurred during Los Angeles’ Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders. Nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains along with turf toe on the Rams’ final offensive play of the afternoon. He was subsequently placed on injured reserve.

This is an especially difficult development for a Rams offense that has struggled to keep its playmakers healthy. Nacua had already missed time earlier in the season with a hip injury, making this another significant setback in an injury-plagued campaign.

Through seven games, Nacua recorded 70 receptions for 715 yards and four touchdowns. His absence leaves Matthew Stafford without one of the NFL’s most productive and reliable receivers.

The Rams will now have to prepare for the possibility of finishing the season without their star wideout. While a return before the end of the year has not been completely ruled out, McVay’s latest update certainly makes that possibility much less encouraging.

item.title: Rams' Puka Nacua not the first NFL player to serve suspension while on IR
item.description: Nacua will eligible to be reinstated ahead of Week 15.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's decision to allow Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua to serve his three-game suspension while on injured reserve raised some eyebrows, but was not an unprecedented decision.

Nacua will serve his ban for violating the league's personal conduct policy as he remains on IR with knee and turf toe injuries. He will be eligible for reinstatement on Dec. 14 as the Rams begin preparations for their Week 15 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, but the team now expects him to miss the remainder of the season after he underwent surgery to repair his right MCL.

Per the NFL, suspensions begin as soon as the discipline is handed down. Nacua was already set to miss the Rams' upcoming games against the Green Bay Packers, Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers. He can be activated from IR at the same time the ban ends.

It's not the first time that a player's suspension will coincide with time spent on IR. There have been four other occasions since 2017 where no game time ended up being missed.

DT David Parry, New Orleans Saints (2017)

Parry was suspended four games in December 2017 after being arrested the previous February while a member of the Indianapolis Colts. The defensive tackle was arrested on charges of auto theft, robbery, resisting arrest, driving under the influence and criminal damage. He played just one game in 2017 after suffering a season-ending ankle injury in Week 1. His suspension ran for the final four games of the regular season, beginning with Week 14, while he was on IR.

WR Michael Woods, Cleveland Browns (2023)

Woods had already been ruled out for the 2023 season after rupturing his Achilles in the offseason. The NFL did not announce his suspension until Week 13, making it a six-game ban for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy.

DE Sam Williams, Dallas Cowboys (2024)

Williams was suspended three games in 2024 after bring arrested on charges of reckless driving, possession of a controlled substance and the unlawful carrying of a weapon in August 2023. He was already on season-ending IR as he was recovering from ACL and MCL tears.

DT Daniel Ekuale, Pittsburgh Steelers (2025)

The NFL handed down a five-game ban for violating the league's performance-enhancing substances policy. Done for the season and on IR after tearing an ACL in Week 8, Ekuale did not miss any games.

Puka Nacua's suspension details

Nacua's suspension comes after he faced a civil lawsuit from a woman over an alleged biting incident and antisemitic comments earlier this year. An attorney representing Nacua denied the woman's claim that he made the antisemitic comment while downplaying the bite mark he left on her. The wide receiver later entered a holistic care facility after facing the off-field allegations.

The NFL reportedly told Nacua that any further violations of the personal conduct policy, "including failure to satisfy his diversion program," will subject him to further discipline, including potential banishment from the league.

The only cost for Nacua will be missing out on $950,000 in salary, according to ESPN's Field Yates.

item.title: Puka Nacua’s nightmare season gets worse as his Rams season is lost
item.description: Rams star Puka Nacua underwent surgery on his injured right knee and is expected to miss the rest of the regular season.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams were already preparing to survive without Puka Nacua for several weeks. Now, they might have to finish the regular season without him altogether.

Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed Friday morning that his star wide receiver underwent surgery to repair the sprained posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) in his right knee and is expected to miss approximately two months, effectively ending his regular season.

It’s another devastating blow for an injury-ravaged Rams team that has spent much of the season watching its biggest stars trade their uniforms for street clothes.

“We always thought [it] was a possibility,” McVay said of Nacua needing surgery. “It’s going to be a couple months and we’re going to have to go on without him.”

McVay wouldn’t rule out the possibility of Nacua returning for the NFL Playoffs, but said the team will operate week to week with the expectation that he won’t be back with the Rams this season.

Puka Nacua’s nightmare season takes another turn

The timing couldn’t be much worse for Nacua, who was already sidelined with multiple injuries to his right knee and turf toe suffered during the Rams’ Week 9 victory over the Washington Commanders.

The Rams initially resisted placing Nacua on injured reserve before reversing course ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Now, what began as a four-game absence has turned into a potentially season-ending injury.

And the surgery comes just days after the NFL handed Nacua a three-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy.

The suspension, which could reportedly lead to banishment from the league, negotiated between the NFL and NFL Players Association, allows Nacua to serve his punishment while on injured reserve, meaning the disciplinary clock continues ticking even as he recovers from surgery.

Perhaps the cruelest twist is the financial timing.

Nacua is playing in the final year of his rookie contract, with a potentially lucrative new deal awaiting him. His suspension will cost him three game checks, but considerably less than it might have under a new contract.

For the Rams, the immediate concern is football. With Davante Adams also sidelined by a hamstring injury, Matthew Stafford is running out of proven weapons as Los Angeles fights to remain in the NFC playoff race.

And for Nacua, a season that was supposed to strengthen his case for a massive payday has instead become a painful combination of injuries, controversy and uncertainty.

This is a developing story with more to follow.

item.title: Eagles opposing player to stop, Week 11 edition
item.description: Philadelphia must take advantage of Pittsburgh’s aging QB.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles have managed to become No. 1 in something in the NFL this season. They currently hold the longest losing streak in the league at seven-straight games, after the Los Angeles Chargers won their first of the season in Baltimore on Monday night.

But the Eagles will be primed to have another streak snapped this Sunday, when they host in-state Pittsburgh Steelers at 1 p.m. at Lincoln Financial Field in a game that flexed up from a nationally televised 4:25 p.m. start to the regionalized 1 p.m. start. The Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since October 24, 1965, winning 20–14 at Franklin Field.

Lyndon Johnson was president, and it was two stadiums and 61 years ago. Eagles own an 11-game home winning streak over the Steelers, going 3-0 at Franklin Field, 4-0 at Veterans Stadium and 4-0 at Lincoln Financial Field. The tie-in with this game is that falls tragically on November 22, the annual anniversary of the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, who was succeeded by Johnson.

Currently, the Steelers have an AFC North Division title to play for, and the Eagles are fighting to work their up the draft order by continuing to lose. It looks like the return of receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks this week against the Steelers, but they will both still have Joltin’ Joe Melton throwing to them, which gives the Eagles a greater chance to lose. There may be as much black-and-gold as midnight green in the stands.

The NFC East is deplorable this season, though it is the Eagles who sit at the bottom, which speaks volumes as to how bad their situation is.   

Adding to that will be facing future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers this weekend.

Rodgers is 42, but even he would be a considerable upgrade as to who the Eagles have now at quarterback. He’s thrown 15 touchdowns against six interceptions this season, completing 190 of 317 passes for 2,014 yards. Rodgers has also been sacked been sacked 26 times, which is the sixth highest in the NFL this season.      

Not that it will help the Eagles, who are 28th in the NFL in sacks with 16 for minus-104 yards, which is 26th in the NFL.

Rodgers may not be able to move like he once did, but he is good enough to beat the Eagles.

Eagles’ defensive coordinator Vic Fangio has seen his share of Rodgers through the years and thinks that the ancient one is still dangerous.

“Yeah, obviously I’ve seen a lot of him over the years,” Fangio said about Rodgers. “I mean, I don’t think anybody can make a top five list of quarterbacks all time without him on it. Just a very pretty passer, great release, super knowledgeable, great anticipation. Just a guy I have a total lot of respect for.”

When asked this week if Rodgers brings an advantage at the line of scrimmage, will he make it more difficult on the Eagles’ defense, especially with his ability to get free plays by drawing defenses offsides.

“Yeah, it can,” Fangio said. “He’s really good at it. He does a great job with the cadence and making you think the play’s ready to go and then pull out of there and change it when you’ve played as long as he has. And now he’s back with [Steelers Head Coach] Mike [McCarthy] in the same system he grew up in. So, it’s like back to the good old days.”

The Eagles are in a state of making things look good, making them seem competitive.

They are arguably the worst team in the NFL and aiming for a higher pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, knowing this season is lost.

Offensively, the Eagles are the worst team in the NFL, with 2,342 yards of total offense, which translates into a season-low 260.2 yards a game average. Staying consistent, the Eagles are the 25th-ranked defense in the NFL, giving up 353.4 yards a game.

Two weeks ago, the New York Giants snapped their 13-game losing streak at Lincoln Financial Field, while the Eagles lost their seventh-straight game, bringing them closer to that magic number of 12-straight losses. The longest Eagles’ losing streak in the Super Bowl era is 11-straight games, which goes to the infamous 1968 Eagles, who lost their first 11 games that season.

The 2026 Eagles are in the running for records.

Now, it is the Steelers’ turn to break an 11-game, 61-year losing streak by beating the hapless Eagles.

The Eagles remain consistent this season.  

Consistently bad.

item.title: Jets improved their special teams coverage by having fullback Andrew Beck handle kickoffs
item.description: Only one kickoff has been returned for a touchdown in the NFL this season, and it was allowed by the Jets when kicker Austin McNamara not only failed to make the tackle, but got in the way of his teammates as they tried to run down Raiders return man Dylan Laube.
item.content:encoded:
Only one kickoff has been returned for a touchdown in the NFL this season, and it was allowed by the Jets when kicker Austin McNamara not only failed to make the tackle, but got in the way of his teammates as they tried to run down Raiders return man Dylan Laube. That got the Jets thinking they needed to improve their kickoff coverage.

The solution was taking kickoff duties away from both McNamara, who is the Jets' punter, and Jason Sanders, who is the Jets' field goal kicker. Instead, it's now fullback Andrew Beck, who has been a good special teams player for years in the NFL, who is handling kickoffs. Beck made a tackle last week on what could have been a much longer kickoff return without him, and he said he loves being able to both kick and make the tackle afterward.

“It was the whole reason that I’m out there, and I think it proves that it’s beneficial to have me doing it,” Beck told Newsday. “Instead of just to get some cool pictures, I’m actually out there doing it for a reason.”

Jets coach Aaron Glenn said when players have a skill set like Beck, with the ability to both kick and tackle, teams need to take advantage of that.

“He’s a unique player that has done a little bit of everything throughout his career,” Glenn said. “We want to utilize that as much as we can.”

Beck kicked in high school but not in college, and he didn't think he'd be kicking again in the NFL. Now that he has the job, however, he hopes it increases his value to the team, and bolsters his career.

“I think I’ve shown that I can be successful in a couple different positions,” he said. “Hopefully the coaches feel comfortable putting me there.”

It's almost unheard of for a player whose primary job isn't punter or kicker to handle kickoffs, although with the dynamic kickoff rule promoting returns, it makes sense for a player who can make tackles to be out there if he's capable of kicking the ball into the landing zone reliably. Saints safety Justin Reid has also kicked off, although he's only done it once this season. If the Jets have success with Beck, it might be something that other teams try — and it might make players who have the unique skill set of being both good kickers and good tacklers more valuable.

item.title: 3 things about Denver Broncos heading into Week 11
item.description: Denver is hot going into Raiders’ matchup
item.content:encoded:
The Las Vegas Raiders head to play at the Denver Broncos on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 1:25 p.m. PT.

Here are three things to know about the Broncos:

They’re rolling:

The 7-2 Broncos have won five straight games. The Broncos have also had the Raiders’ number lately as they have beaten them four consecutive games. That came directly after the Raiders won eight straight games over Denver.

They’re struggling on the ground:

The Broncos aren’t running the ball well. They are averaging 81.4 yards a game on the ground and just 3.7 yards per carry. The Raiders’ defense has been gutted by the run, but they may get a break this week against the Broncos.

Bo Nix gets hot when he has to:

Denver quarterback Bo Nix isn’t perfect, but he gets hot when the game is on the line. They have three fourth-quarter comebacks wins this season and have won 16 straight one-score games.

The Saints defense ranks sixth in half PPR points allowed to TEs at 13.1 per game, and they don't have the LB/S play to worry about. Harold Fannin Jr. had one of the best reps of the season against them in Week 9, and Isaiah Likely hung 99-1 on them over their last month of games. Chicago enters as 11.5-point home favorites with an implied team total of 30 points (fourth).

Patrick Mahomes (vs. ARI) - 20.4 proj. points

Mahomes exploded for 348 yards and five passing touchdowns against Atlanta in Week 10, bringing his season-long baseline up to QB6 (20.8 PPG). He has delivered +0.15 EPA per dropback (QB9) across his nine starts while chipping in 11.1 rushing yards per game (28th). I can make the case that the return of Rashee Rice and the addition of Josh Downs have the pass game in the best spot of the year right now.

Plus, the Cardinals defense can't stop anyone, allowing the third-most fantasy points to QBs this season. Matthew Stafford turned in three scores despite missing his top receivers last week, and Dak Prescott (QB11), Bo Nix (QB3) and Jared Goff (QB4) have all lit it up since September. It's not a surprise to see the Chiefs projected for 28.5 points (sixth). They won't have Kenneth Walker (groin), which could mean additional throwing production on the margins.

This assumes Jalon Daniels is back at QB with Baker Mayfield (foot) picking up a new injury during the bye week. That's too big to fail, especially given how slippery he is on tape.

The Lions are a pass funnel typically, but the losses of LB Jack Campbell, EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and CB D.J. Reed (questionable) make them fairly bad in both phases. They still have some DTs to worry about, but the Bucs should be able to run it here, despite the spreadsheets suggesting otherwise. Tampa Bay will attempt to bleed out the clock as 7-point road dogs with a team total of 18.25 points (21st). Irving should absorb a lot of that team total.

Tetairoa McMillan (vs. BAL) - 63.5 proj. receiving yards

McMillan is averaging 8.2 half PPR points on 11.7 expected points in his eight games with Jalen Coker this year. Over the past month against a more difficult schedule, he's the WR53 on WR25 usage. He hasn't been getting as open of late, and then Bryce Young has missed him up the sideline a bit too often. He's still handling 24% of targets in an offense that leans pass-first in neutral situations, but the alpha WR1 traits haven't fully blossomed in his second season. He's a very good, not elite, WR to me.

The Ravens sent home podcaster Marlon Humphrey, not that he was very good in coverage this year. He'll battle with CB1 Nate Wiggins, who is much lighter but much faster than McMillan. Brown to compete with, he also plays in a bottom-5 offense now. It's hard to calibrate all of the moving pieces, so Smith is a boom-bust WR3 until we have a better clue for how Joe Milton is going to fit in with Smith.

On top of that, the Steelers have an excellent DL that can spoil the entire game. Philly only has a 17.5-point team total, and I totally get it.

item.title: Detroit Lions name a new captain on defense
item.description: The Detroit Lions have a new captain in veteran safety Chuck Clark.
item.content:encoded:
As first reported by Justin Rogers and confirmed by coach Dan Campbell on Friday, the Detroit Lions have a new defensive captain. Veteran safety Chuck Clark was given the honors earlier this week, after the Lions had lost two defensive captains to injury over the past three weeks: Jack Campbell (neck), Aidan Hutchinson (knee).

“It felt like the right thing to do,” Campbell said. “We obviously lost a couple of our captains. He’s really just filled the void as the season has gone on. Type of guy he is, it just speaks for itself. And he’s just grown inside this locker room, he’s a great teammate, and he’s just got leadership qualities through the room. Communication is outstanding. His production has gone up as the season’s gone up. Everybody’s got a lot of faith in Chuck. He’s just kinda one of those bell-cow guys for us right now. So he earned that, so proud of him.”

Clark is in his 10th NFL season and first with the Lions. Campbell noted that they knew about Clark’s leadership qualities before they signed him to a one-year, $1.5 million deal this offseason, but you never know for sure until he’s actually in the building. Thus far, he’s lived up to his reputation.

“You get around him and you see it first hand. There’s nothing fake about it. He’s just real,” Campbell said. “He’s one of those guys that people gravitate to him. He’s just got it. He’s a great communicator, same guy every day, very consistent, smart, grinder. He’s everything you really want in that type of role.”

In addition to his leadership, Clark has become an important part of the gameday lineup. He’s been a steadying force in Detroit’s ever-shifting secondary, logging more defensive snaps (540) than anyone else on the team. And while his role may soon decrease with the return of Brian Branch a few weeks ago and Kerby Joseph this week, Campbell noted that they want to still use all of their safeties, Clark included.

“Everybody’ got a role. We’re trying to use everybody that we can in that defensive room. So all those safeties? We want to use them,” Campbell said. “There’s a role for all of those guys. And now you get Kerby back in the fold. So we’ve got a couple of things that we can do here and have flexibility to do.”

item.title: Kingdom Keys: 3 Keys to a Chiefs victory over the Cardinals in Week 11
item.description: Kansas City must keep its receivers rolling, rattle Carson Beck and build an early lead before its coming gauntlet.
item.content:encoded:
Kansas City hosts the injury-depleted Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in what should be another very winnable game. The Chiefs are 7-2 and tied with the Denver Broncos atop the AFC West, one game behind the Buffalo Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Arizona is 3-7, has lost consecutive games, and is coming off a 34-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

After Sunday, Kansas City begins a five-game stretch against Buffalo, the Los Angeles Rams, Cincinnati, New England and San Francisco. The first three games of that stretch will be on the road, beginning with a Thanksgiving night matchup against the Bills just four days after the Cardinals game.

The Chiefs cannot afford to overlook Arizona, but they should use this matchup to prepare themselves for what is coming.

Here are three Kingdom Keys to a Chiefs victory.

Offensive key: Keep building chemistry with the wide receivers.

Kansas City’s wide receivers delivered their best collective performance of the season against Atlanta.

Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Cyrus Allen, and Andrew Armstrong combined for 12 receptions, 222 yards and three touchdowns. Rice led the group with five catches for 82 yards, while Downs caught four passes for 53 yards and a touchdown in his Chiefs debut.

Allen and Armstrong also delivered explosive touchdown receptions of 39 and 43 yards, respectively. The receivers accounted for nearly 64% of Patrick Mahomes’ 348 passing yards and three of his five touchdown passes.

That production must become the start of a trend rather than a one-game explosion.

Downs had only two full practices with Mahomes before the Atlanta game. Sunday offers another chance to build that connection while continuing to define roles for Rice, Allen and Armstrong. It would also be encouraging to get Worthy involved after he went without a reception on three targets against the Falcons.

Arizona presents an ideal matchup for that continued growth. The Cardinals have allowed 22 passing touchdowns — tied for the second-most in the NFL — and are surrendering 28.9 points per game.

The Chiefs will need their receivers during the upcoming stretch against several playoff contenders. Buffalo, Los Angeles, Cincinnati, New England and San Francisco will all have defensive plans designed to slow Kansas City’s running game and force the receivers to win their matchups.

Another combined 150-yard performance from the wide-receiver room would qualify as a successful afternoon. More importantly, Kansas City needs the group to keep building timing and trust with Mahomes before the schedule’s difficulty increases.

Defensive key: Force Carson Beck into multiple turnovers

The Chiefs’ defense has been one of the league’s best at keeping opponents out of the end zone.

Kansas City is allowing only 17.3 points per game, third-best in the NFL, and has surrendered just 13 touchdowns through nine games. The defense has also generated 13 takeaways and owns a plus-six turnover differential.

This week should provide an opportunity to add to that total.

Arizona traded Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in October and dealt veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore before the trade deadline. Starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II, rookie running back Jeremiyah Love and wide receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne are among the Cardinals currently on injured reserve. Arizona has 16 players on injury lists, tied for the most in the league.

Trey McBride remains a dangerous target at tight end, but Arizona’s offense is otherwise relying heavily on inexperienced players and reserves.

Rookie quarterback Carson Beck will make his second NFL start after struggling against the Rams. Beck completed 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards, threw two interceptions, lost a fumble and was sacked five times. Arizona finished with only 123 total yards and failed to convert any of its six third-down opportunities.

Steve Spagnuolo should disguise coverages, change the picture after the snap and force Beck to process quickly. Pressure will be important, but the defensive backs must also capitalize when the rookie puts the football in danger.

The Chiefs forced two turnovers against Atlanta. Reaching that number again should be the defensive benchmark against Arizona.

X-factor: Win early and protect the roster

The X-factor is not simply winning the game. It is winning efficiently enough to protect the roster for what comes next.

Kansas City already has several important players dealing with injuries. Kenneth Walker III missed the Atlanta game with a groin injury, while Trey Smith remains in the concussion protocol and Jaylon Moore is working through an ankle injury. Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice have also appeared on the injury report, although each practiced fully on Wednesday.

The Chiefs cannot control whether every player avoids injury, but they can reduce unnecessary exposure by taking command of the game early.

Kansas City should aim to establish a three-score advantage by the middle of the third quarter. That would give Andy Reid an opportunity to reduce the workloads of Mahomes, Kelce, Rice, Chris Jones and other important veterans during the second half.

This is particularly important because the Chiefs will have only four days to prepare for Buffalo. After that Thanksgiving matchup, they will remain on the road to face the Rams the following Thursday and Cincinnati 10 days later.

The Chiefs cannot let Arizona hang around into the fourth quarter. A comfortable lead would allow them to rest starters, give younger players valuable snaps and begin shifting their attention toward the most demanding portion of their schedule.

The bottom line

The Cardinals’ record and depleted roster make this a game Kansas City should control, but its importance extends beyond one victory.

The Chiefs need another strong showing from their wide receivers as they continue building chemistry for the upcoming gauntlet. Defensively, they should exploit an inexperienced quarterback and force at least two turnovers. Most importantly, Kansas City needs to build an early lead and get its most valuable players off the field once the result is secure.

If the Chiefs accomplish those three things, they should improve to 8-2 while entering their Thanksgiving showdown with Buffalo healthy, confident and still positioned to compete for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.

item.title: Cowboys vs Titans: 3 causes for concern in Week 11
item.description: The Cowboys need a win in the worst way
item.content:encoded:
The Dallas Cowboys are back in action Sunday afternoon, hosting their second of three straight home games as they welcome the Tennessee Titans to town. While the Titans enter the matchup with a 1-8 record, nothing the Cowboys have shown this season suggests this will be an easy game.

With that thought in mind, here are three causes for concern in Sunday’s matchup.

1) Cam Ward Flashing His Potential 

Former number one overall pick Cam Ward’s NFL career has not gotten off to the best start. Ward showed some flashes during his rookie year but struggled with consistency. Playing behind arguably the league’s worst offensive line, Ward was sacked a league-high 55 times during his first season.

Despite some of the struggles he endured last season, expectations were high for the Miami product entering year two. Most of Ward’s second year in the league hasn’t been much better than his first. This season, the 24-year-old has thrown just eight touchdown passes in nine games to go with a disappointing 53.3 QBR.

While Ward and the Titans as a whole have not had an ideal season, to say the least, the past two weeks have been much better on the offensive side of the ball. Tennessee’s signal-caller has been the main reason why, as the talented young quarterback has played arguably his best two games of the year in back-to-back weeks.

Over the course of the last two weeks, Ward is second in the NFL in completion percentage (70.9) to go with four touchdown passes and a very impressive 98.9 Passer Rating. While the Titans have not won either of these contests, their offense has not been the reason why, as they have recorded 325 or more yards in each matchup. 

With Ward playing as well as we’ve seen him since he entered the league, the Cowboys need to be on high alert and not let the young quarterback get into a rhythm on Sunday afternoon.

2) Titans’ Defense Takeaway Surge

Like the Cowboys, the Titans have been one of the worst defenses in football this season. Tennessee has given up the sixth-most points (239) in the league, allowing at least 26 points in four of their last five matchups.

While the Titans have not done much well on defense this season, since Week 6 they have been one of the better defenses in the league at taking the football away from their opponent. Tennessee’s defense has 10 takeaways in their last four matchups, including two or more in three straight games from Week 6 through Week 8. The one win the Titans recorded this season came in Week 6 when they recorded three takeaways in a 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts.

One positive for Dallas is that four of those 10 takeaways came via safety Amani Hooker. The 28-year-old, who was without a doubt the top takeaway threat on the Titans’ defense, was traded to the Buffalo Bills before the trade deadline two weeks ago.

Taking care of the football is going to be paramount for the Cowboys on Sunday. The Titans have plenty of defensive weaknesses they should be able to exploit, but if they don’t protect the ball, Tennessee could make it a long day for Dallas’ offense.

3) Internal Defensive Chaos

As is usually the case, there is a bit of chaos surrounding the Cowboys. Earlier this week, Dallas made the decision to take play-calling duties away from first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker, giving the job to 60-year-old Mike Pettine.

With how bad Dallas’ defense has been, giving play-calling duties to Pettine, the veteran coach was brought in a few weeks back to be a defensive consultant; this should not come as a surprise, but the decision has stirred up some internal drama. Parker himself admitted he contemplated leaving the organization altogether after the decision was made, while Dallas’ star defender Quinnen Williams refused to answer questions on the matter this week.

It’s been quite the week in Dallas, and the Cowboys’ issues on defense seem to be extending off the field as well. It will be very interesting to see if the events of this week have any impact on the field this weekend.
