item.title: Week 11 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets for this week's games
item.description: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 11 games.
item.content:encoded:
Week 11 of the NFL season began with the Houston Texans taking care of business and easily defeating the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday night.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 11 of the NFL season.

Odds subject to change.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-6.5, 45.5)

Jacob: How flawless was Lions quarterback Jared Goff through the first six games of the 2026 season?

He put the ball in the air 223 times and not once did it land in the hands of the wrong team. In the past three games, though, Goff has gotten quite charitable. He threw one interception against Minnesota in Week 8, one against Miami in Week 9 and two against New England a week ago in Germany. In all, four INTs in his last 81 pass attempts.

The good news for Goff: He hasn't been picked off in four straight games in more than four seasons (Weeks 3-7 in 2022). The bad news: This week, the 2016 No. 1 overall pick is facing a Tampa Bay defense that has recorded an NFL-high 16 INTs.

In their most recent game — a 27-24 Week 9 loss at Chicago — the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times. They did the same thing the previous week to Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. And in the five games prior, Tampa intercepted every QB it faced at least once.

In fact, the Buccaneers' defense has nabbed at least one interception in eight of nine games. And oddsmakers are offering plus money that they won't do the same thing against a suddenly turnover-prone Goff? Take it.

Bet: Jared Goff over 1.5 interceptions (+121)

Pond: Despite the fact Baker Mayfield (foot sprain) returned to practice in a limited capacity Thursday, he will be far from 100 percent if he takes the field against the Lions.

Without a mobile Mayfield, I would imagine head coach Todd Bowles will resort to his two-headed, top-ranked ground attack featuring Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell. The Buccaneers took this approach two weeks back when the pair combined for a jaw-dropping 52 carries and 310 yards on the ground in a 16-0 rain-soaked win against Atlanta.

With that likely game plan, Tampa Bay will do all it can to control the clock and keep Goff and the Detroit offense off the field. And that means we could see a low-scoring affair at Ford Field.

Six of the Buccaneers' past eight games have seen a combined total of 45 points or less, so I'm taking a shot that their methodical offense and top-ranked defense can keep this one close.

Bet: Under 46.5 points alt total (-115, FanDuel)

New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5, 49.5)

Russell: In the NFL, absence makes the heart grow fonder, or, in the case of the Bears, it makes the betting market forget about four interceptions by Caleb Williams, and a non-spread-covering win over the Buccaneers. At least that's what this point spread indicates, as it's five points clear of the Bears last-known betting line,  against Tampa Bay. 

The Bears, with added pieces to their defense and a thrill-a-minute offense, are the darlings of the NFC at the moment. The type of thing that happens when you win three straight games, all in primetime. The result? A rating in the betting market that makes Chicago the perceived best team in the NFL. 

There are four other double-digit point spreads in Week 11. Three of them involve rookie quarterbacks, and the fourth was Daniel Jones and the Colts at Houston. This is not that. 

Coming into Thursday night, Jones was 29th out of 31 qualifying quarterbacks in adjusted EPA/Play, while Tyler Shough is slotted in the middle of the NFL pack. 

Unlike the Colts — or the Cardinals, Dolphins and Raiders — the Saints are actually getting healthier as the season goes on, with the return of left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr., first-round pick Jordan Tyson and No. 1 tailback Travis Etienne in the past two weeks. Needing overtime to beat Shedeur Sanders and the Browns at home and a loss to the Panthers (on a last-second 54-yard field goal), hasn't helped market perception of New Orleans, but judging the Saints off the entire season has made them underrated.

Especially since a somewhat healthy version won at Baltimore and almost did so at Detroit in their first two games, showing what they're capable of at full strength.

Bet: Saints +11.5

Jacksonville Jaguars (-5.5, 46.5) at New York Giants

Jacob: New York's offense has been far more productive this season than expected — particularly considering the team's merry-go-round at quarterback. While cycling through Jaxson Dart, Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy, the Giants have put up at least 19 points in seven of nine games.

The exceptions: a 28-6 Week 2 loss at the Rams (the game where Dart suffered his season-ending knee injury) and a 12-7 Week 3 win over the Titans. Overall, New York has topped 20 points seven times and tallied at least 27 five times.

Now for the "but": Of the eight teams the Giants have played, only one currently ranks in the top 18 in scoring defense. That team? The Rams (who, to repeat, held New York to two field goals). Including two games against Washington, the Giants' opponents enter this week with the following scoring-defense rankings: fifth (Rams), 18th, 19th, 20th, 26th, 28th, 30th and 31st.

New York's Week 11 foe? It fields the NFL's second-stingiest defense. Not only does Jacksonville yield just 16 points per game, but only five opponents have eclipsed 10 points; only three have cleared 17; and only two have topped 20 (Houston put up 34 in London in Week 6, and Tennessee scored 23 last week).

The only other team to exceed 20 points against Jacksonville in the last 17 games — 15 of which the Jags have won? Arizona (24 points in an overtime loss in Week 12 last season).

McCarthy and the Giants are unlikely to join that list Sunday, especially in what are expected to be soggy conditions at MetLife Stadium.

Bet: Giants under 20.5 total points (-130)

Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3.5, 46.5)

Pond: You couldn't ask for a better Sunday night clash than this showdown between NFC powerhouses in Mexico City. And it will pit San Francisco's explosive offense against Minnesota's stingy defense, which concedes just 14 PPG.

The 49ers have been the poster child for first-half dominance, not trailing once at the break and boasting an 8-0-1 record through 30 minutes of play. MVP candidate Brock Purdy and RB Christian McCaffrey have this San Francisco offense clicking right out of the gate, which I expect to be the case again.

Meanwhile, the Vikings look like a completely different team with the return of Kirk Cousins under center. As my colleague Ben Fawkes reported, Minnesota has been popular in Super Bowl futures wagering after its 30-10 dismantling of Green Bay last week at Lambeau Field.

As for the total, we're going to see some tired legs late in this game due to the unforgiving altitude (7,352 feet above sea level) in Mexico City.

Combining the thin-air angle and Minnesota having the league's best defense leads me to believe Kevin O'Connell's outfit will have a big second-half advantage, putting it in position to win this game outright.

Expect a tale of two halves in a close game where points will be at a premium.

Bets: 49ers 1H ML (-115) | Vikings +3.5 (-118) | Under 47.5 (-130) at FanDuel

item.title: Fan, 36, dies after violent 49ers, Cowboys brawls at AT&T Stadium
item.description: A 36-year-old man has passed away following a fight at the 49ers-Cowboys game.
item.content:encoded:
A fan who attended the San Francisco 49ers vs. Dallas Cowboys game at AT&T Stadium this past weekend has passed away.

The Independent reported on Friday that a 36-year-old fan named Mario Narro died in the hospital several days after getting into a fight with a fan during the 49ers-Cowboys game.

The alleged fight took place around kickoff of the game. The man remained at the game but was complaining of pain.

He was later taken to a hospital and eventually passed away on Wednesday.

It’s unclear who the man was fighting, and whether the man was a fan of the 49ers or the Cowboys. A graphic paying tribute to the man was posted on social media that showed him wearing a CeeDee Lamb Cowboys jersey, but that is not confirmed.

There were several brawls that surfaced on social media in the wake of San Francisco’s 46-40 win.

49ers fans have been involved in multiple fights over the past few weeks, including several that went viral after San Francisco beat the Las Vegas Raiders at Levi’s Stadium two weekends ago.

There was one video that surfaced of a fight outside of AT&T Stadium this past weekend, which eventually led to two police officers needing to get involved. But its unclear whether any arrests were made or what charges any people involved in the brawl might have faced.

item.title: Fantasy Football: These NFL teams are dead in the water — but can we still trust their stars in our lineups?
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Chris Allen examines some bottom-barrel teams as we head into Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
My wife and I were huge fans of "The Walking Dead" in its prime. She avoids scary movies like the plague. Yet, the drama kept us both locked in on Sundays until (spoiler alert) we lost Glenn. Afterward, we kept watching because it was our routine. But it didn't feel the same. And once we found something else, we never really noticed we had fallen behind on the show.

We've got several teams with the same vibe. Injuries or trades have erased any playoff hopes. And sure, there's still a player or two on the roster I'm looking to for fantasy production. But we need talent AND situation for that, and we don't have time to wait and see if things will change.

So, let's go through the teams that are (likely) dead and figure out which of their guys we can finally let go.

Cardinals – Trey McBride

Honestly, speaking of "The Walking Dead," Arizona's roster probably looks like that group photo of the cast from Season 1 with most of the people grayed out because they were killed off during the show. The Cardinals have 14 players on IR. Jacoby Brissett is in Baltimore. And our lone ray of hope for Trey McBride is that Carson Beck immediately looked for him during his first start last Sunday.

Carson Beck's first NFL pass is complete to Trey McBride for a first down

LARvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/EOAdAg7BGm

— NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026

There's a two-pronged, glass-half-full spin for McBride's value as we enter the Beck Era. First, all of his targets were first-read looks. Not a single throw from Beck to his TE1 took more than 2.2 seconds to get there. And, two, every single one of them was on the mark (100% catchable target rate). The problem was how every other facet of the offense operated.

  • CPOE: +0.9% (w/  Brissett), -9.4% (w/ Beck)

  • Dropbacks per Game: 44.1, 24.0

  • Offensive Plays per Game: 68.6, 34.0

Granted, trying to avoid Aaron Donald and Braden Fiske carries its own challenge. But just 18 pass attempts will be what craters McBride's case to stay in the TE1 conversation. Jacoby Brissett threw the ball 20 times in his last game for Arizona. Sure, he wound up benched afterward, but McBride hasn't earned five targets in a single game since Week 16 of '24.

If you want to blame the schedule, I'll grant you that. Plus, the Cardinals have some easier matchups for Beck after their Week 14 bye (at NYJ, vs. NO, at LV). Accordingly, you could use the potential of improved environments for the Cardinals offense during the playoff stretch as a means to put McBride in a deal before the default deadline next week.

Patriots – Rhamondre Stevenson

By and large, RBs are at the mercy of their QB's passing ability. All but four of the rushers with top-12 marks in red-zone touches come from top-12 squads in EPA per dropback. You need breakaway speed like Bijan Robinson or Jonathan Taylor to overcome a poor situation. That's not Rhamondre Stevenson's game. And New England's offensive ecosystem just took a turn for the worse. 

Roger McCreary Picks Off Tommy DeVito.

Genuinely, Where Was He Throwing This Ball? He Literally Threw It Right To The Defender.

The Patriots Are Cooked. pic.twitter.com/lyqrnGuMnR

— SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 15, 2026

Tommy DeVito didn't complete a pass farther than six air yards when he came in relief for Drake Maye. And I realize honing in on a single play misses some context around the entire performance. But DeVito didn't see other throwing windows anyway. Besides, that wasn't his only problem.

  • Pressure Rate: 48.4%, 3rd (highest rate of any single game for NE)

  • Pressure-to-Sack Ratio: 26.7%, 1st 

  • Quick Pressure Rate: 33.3%, 10th 

Without DE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions were only able to get to DeVito soon after the snap on just a third of his dropbacks. But even when granted a clean pocket, he barely completed more than half of his attempts. The offense averaged 32.9 yards per drive with Maye during their gauntlet stretch of high-end defenses to start the year. It was down to 12.1 after he left the game.

That's why I'd be looking to move Stevenson. Corey Kiner's expanded role is just icing on the cake. He was already taking a third of the carries during the month prior. Stevenson's only upside was as a receiver. But if the Patriots have a bad backup QB and a tough schedule on the horizon (Bills in Week 13, Vikings, Chiefs), I'd rather let somebody else take on the risk. 

Dolphins – Ollie Gordon II

So, let's apply the same process I laid out for the Patriots to the Dolphins. Essentially, we'll evaluate Miami's passing attack with Kyle McCord running the show as a means to gauge Ollie Gordon II's outlook. Right away, things look better down south. 

Part of Kyle McCord’s game is a pretty, accurate, and catchable deep ball. A big 38-yard play to Caleb Douglas on a beautiful reception for a 1st down. pic.twitter.com/TC6JmAmMEf

— Jason Sarney - Dolphins Wire (@Jason_Sarney) November 15, 2026

Before you call me on trying to lead the witness, I know McCord had a strip-fumble gaffe that turned into six points for the Colts. But he also used his legs to score on a QB draw to cancel things out. Plus, as the above clip emphasizes, McCord pushed the ball farther downfield and took fewer sacks. Remember that 12.1 YPD metric for DeVito? McCord was up to 27.5. Overall, we can put the Dolphins' passing game ahead of New England's. Now, let's look at Gordon's workload.

  • Rushing Share (since Week 4): 71%, 9th (out of 30 RBs – min. 150 snaps)

  • Short-Yardage Rate: 88%, 5th

  • Target Share: 8%, 21st 

At 17.8 carries per game, Gordon has one of the strongest opportunity shares in the league. Only James Cook III has seen a higher stacked box rate on early downs than Gordon (46.8%), but the Dolphins' RB1 isn't lagging too far behind in adjusted yards after contact per attempt (3.79 vs 3.15) or rushing success rate (46.3% vs 39.4%). And outside of Denver, no rushing defense on Miami's schedule should give you pause. Unless I could get similar RB2 value for Gordon, I'd keep him.

Chargers – Omarion Hampton

Let me flip the script when talking about Omarion Hampton. He put up his best performance of the season against the Ravens. More importantly, there were enough elements on tape to make the case that we can see something similar in the future.

Joe Alt, Travis Burke, and Jake Slaughter create a hole for Omarion Hampton to burst through for his longest run of the game (19 yards).

Was nice to see some competence from the run game last night after a few brutal weeks. We'll find out how long it lasts, but it was a start. pic.twitter.com/04LBll4y1C

— Alex Insdorf (@alexinsdorf99) November 17, 2026

Hampton has just five carries that have gained 15 or more yards. Kaelon Black, Christian McCaffrey's backup, has the same total. Anyway, two of those five from Hampton came on Monday night. But it wasn't just because the offensive line opened up a couple of holes. Baltimore met Hampton at or behind the LoS on 63.6% of his carries. He responded with a season-high 4.45 adjusted yards after contact per attempt. But we know efficiency can fluctuate between games. If I had a choice, I'd rather the volume hold.

  • Rushing Share: 81.0%, Season-high

  • Target Rate: 13.0%, Season-high

  • Short-Yardage Rate: 75%, second-highest

OC Mike McDaniel finally came (back) around to the idea that letting Hampton lead the backfield was the best option. The line still needs to improve (0.8 yards before contact per attempt), but getting his RB1 into a rhythm has its merits. 

Three of the Chargers' next six opponents are inside the top 10 in PPG allowed to rushers. The same number of defensive fronts are below the league average in pressure rate, giving Justin Herbert more time in the pocket and keeping the offense on schedule. If you could acquire Hampton off the 3-7 or 4-6 team without sacrificing much, I'd send out an offer for him.

Colts – Jonathan Taylor

Let's be real for a minute. The Colts underperforming was a risk we all accepted when drafting Jonathan Taylor. Daniel Jones was coming off of the Achilles reconstruction. Alec Pierce's health was in question even during the summer. Admittedly, a franchise-altering implosion wasn't easy to see, but Taylor maintaining his workhorse status was the bet we made in the first round. Indianapolis pulled the rug out from under us two months later. 

2nd push from Indy gets Seth McGowan in for a TD

MIAvsIND on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPluspic.twitter.com/YtxqrK6PMZ

— NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026

Unfortunately, Taylor didn't lose his shoe, leading to another high-value touch for Seth McGowan against the Dolphins. And it wasn't the first time we had to question the workload for their (and our!) RB1. Since Indianapolis opened its doors for business, we've seen less of Taylor in the role we got used to back in September.

  • Snap Rate: 80% (before Nelson trade), 67% (since the trades)

  • Rush Share: 74%, 51% 

  • Goal-line Share: 87%, 60%

Even in TNF to start Week 11, McGowan took 27.6% of the snaps with four touches to Taylor's 10. McGowan primarily played on long-down-and-distance scenarios, but they nearly split the targets (2 to 1), and both were on the field for half of the Colts' red-zone plays. It took a hamstring for McGowan to put Taylor back in the driver's seat.

Taylor was ninth in explosive run rate and one of 10 RBs with a double-digit target rate through Week 6. Simply put, he could overcome a poor environment. But as the Colts look to either preserve Taylor for the offseason trade market or evaluate the rest of the roster, moving on from the RB1 should be in your plans.

item.title: Eagles News: Markel Bell and Philadelphia’s offensive line facing a huge challenge
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles news and links for 11/20/26.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation!

No team has allowed more unblocked pressure this season than the Eagles. Seems like a bad matchup going up against this Pittsburgh pass rush! T.J. Watt vs. Markel Bell could get ugly. It would be an encouraging long-term development to see the rookie tackle rise to the occasion in this matchup.

Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links …

Eagles-Steelers preview: 5 things to watch – PhillyVoice

1) This could be a nightmare day for the Eagles’ offensive line. The Eagles haven’t been able to protect the quarterback all season long, and are coming off a game in which Joe Milton was sacked seven times by a Giants defense that previously only had 10 sacks on the season. The Steelers have one of the best defensive fronts in the NFL, with all kinds of players who can get to the quarterback, most notably T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, and Cameron Heyward. The Steelers will move Watt around a little bit, but he mostly rushes against the RT, where the Eagles had to replace a now retired Lane Johnson with third-round rookie Markel Bell. As noted in our rookie progress report on Monday, Bell has had growing pains in his rookie season, which of course is to be expected. But he also hasn’t yet faced anyone as good as Watt, who has 7.5 sacks this season, and who ranks 31st all-time with 122.5 career sacks. This will be an extremely difficult challenge for Bell, obviously. When the season is over, the Eagles will have to decide if they think Bell showed enough as a rookie to trust him as the starting RT going forward, and this game against Watt could be one that helps make that determination.

Eagles-Steelers Game Preview: 5 questions and answers with the Week 11 enemy – BGN

Can the Philadelphia Eagles make it two weeks in a row where they don’t lose?! Their bye was the easy part of that equation. Now the Birds have to go out and beat the Pittsburgh Steelers to snap a seven-game losing streak. In order to preview this Week 11 Keystone State matchup, I reached out to our enemies over at Behind The Steel Curtain. The ravishing Ryan Parish kindly took the time took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers.

NFC East Mixtape VOL. 208: Is this the week of change? – NFC East Mixtape

Another week is here for the NFC East and this one looks like it could potentially offer legitimate change moving forward. First up the Dallas Cowboys are taking on the Tennessee Titans and for the first time without Christian Parker calling plays… what impact will that even have? The Philadelphia Eagles are hosting their old Steagles friends in the Pittsburgh Steelers… does anything matter anymore? Elsewhere the New York Giants can send a huge statement with a win over the Jacksonville Jaguars… but can they even pull that off? Finally the Washington Commanders have a chance to also make some noise on Monday night against the Cincinnati Bengals… or else their season might end. RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss it all on the latest NFC East Mixtape! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed!

Sean Mannion Update – Iggles Blitz

If Nick Sirianni, Howie Roseman, and Jeffrey Lurie see the right traits in Mannion, they are more likely to be patient with him and let him learn on the fly. Mannion was dealt some tough circumstances with injuries, surprise retirements, and trades. The offense is a shell of what it was supposed to be. That doesn’t excuse the offense being awful, but you have to take everything into consideration when evaluating Mannion and the offense. The test for Mannion now is to see if he was able to take advantage of the bye week and come up with some ways to improve the offense. His focus was improving communication.

Eagles backup DTs ready for opportunity after Jordan Davis trade – NBCSP

Ty Robinson and Byron Young miss Jordan Davis already. They became close to the former Eagles’ first-round pick who was traded to Jacksonville at the trade deadline last week. But they know what that trade means for them: More playing time. “It’s a bittersweet opportunity, obviously, because it sucks losing Jordan, especially in our room,” Robinson said. “But it’s an opportunity for me to get out on the field a little bit more. I’m excited and I’m ready.” In the Eagles’ first nine games of the season, Davis played 323 defensive snaps (52%). Those snaps are now up for grabs. Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said Young and Robinson will play more and then the fifth guy will be either Gabe Hall or Leki Fotu, who are both on the practice squad. Jalen Carter has already been on the field for 84% of the Eagles snaps, so he isn’t going to play more. Moro Ojomo might see a few more snaps but he was already second among the Eagles’ DTs. So the players who will benefit most from these extra opportunities are Young and Robinson. And Fangio said both of them have the ability to play nose tackle in his defense.

NFL Week 11 preview: Picks, predictions, schedule, betting odds, fantasy tips – ESPN

Stat to know: The Eagles’ offense is tied for 30th in the NFL with 16.4 points per game. That ranking would be tied for the team’s worst in scoring in franchise history (they were also 30th in 1998).

NFL Week 11 picks: Upset and score predictions, matchup breakdowns for every game – NFL.com

Why Gennaro picked the Steelers: Because I envision Terrible Towels flying across The Linc in this battle of Pennsylvania. For the first time in the Nick Sirianni era, Philadelphia’s season is over before Thanksgiving. The Eagles entered their Week 10 bye with a seven-game losing streak and came out of it without their best run-stuffer. Eight months after handing Jordan Davis a $78 million extension, Howie Roseman traded the hulking nose tackle for draft currency. Not only did that move underscore the obvious — that Philadelphia is punting on 2026 and planning for the future — but it stripped Vic Fangio’s defense of a key cog against this particular opponent. These Steelers are clearly at their best when the offense runs through Jaylen Warren, who leads all qualified RBs with an average of 5.7 yards per carry. But this past Sunday night, Pittsburgh ran into a Bengals buzzsaw, and Warren was quickly game-scripted out of the blowout loss, finishing with a season-low seven carries. I expect Mike McCarthy to feed his star back early and often against a Philly front that had struggled to stop the run with Davis. Now that the 6-foot-6, 336-pound space-eater is in Jacksonville, Warren is poised for a bounce-back performance. And like I alluded to at the top, this will please the scores of Steelers fans who’ve presumably hoovered up tickets from a downtrodden Eagles fan base.

Bears-Lions Thanksgiving audience will be huge — and it could have been even bigger – PFT

The problem is the second game. The 2-7 Eagles are in soft-tank mode. The 4-6 Cowboys have disintegrated into defensive disarray. While it will still attract a very large audience given the captive audience and the usual Thanksgiving routines, it likely won’t approach 50 million. While the NFL has granted a permanent hammerlock to the Lions and Cowboys for the traditional Thanksgiving afternoon games, a simple tweak would have set the stage for Bears-Lions to break 50 million — and perhaps to threaten last year’s record.

Jaelan Phillips named NFC Defensive Player of the week – Cat Scratch Reader

Congrats to Jaelan Phillips on being named NFC Defensive Player of the Week!

Josiah Deguara: Joins LAC practice squad – CBS Sports

The tight end was cut from Seattle’s practice squad in late October. He did see action in one NFL regular-season game earlier in the year with Philadelphia, playing on 21 special-teams snaps.

NY Giants signed Xavier Gipson to provide ‘spark’ in return game – Big Blue View

EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The New York Giants signed Xavier Gipson off the Philadelphia Eagles’ practice squad this week because they “need a spark” in the kick return game, special teams coordinator Chris Horton said on Thursday.

The Cowboys handled the Christian Parker situation poorly – Blogging The Boys

Nobody is saying that this is the case, but stripping Parker of play-calling duties and giving them to Pettine after a month makes it seem like the move to bring him in wasn’t to help, but rather take his job. The Cowboys praised the hiring of Parker all offseason long, yet they only gave him two months before publicly shaming him in a sense. This is his first time doing this, and it was always going to be a process, but the Cowboys didn’t give him the necessary time to grow into the role. Going back to Eberflus, his unit was atrocious last year. Again, it was the worst in Cowboys’ history up until this season. However, he was never stripped of his duties to call plays, so why do that to Parker? Especially when it’s his first time as a defensive coordinator and play caller. This is just a bad look for the organization starting with the aforementioned Jones, but also Schottenheimer.

Commanders vs. Bengals Thursday injury report: Lucas Patrick is back – Hogs Haven

Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs missed Thursday’s practice, but his absence was not injury related. It was part of his veteran rest schedule. So Diggs was out…and that’s it. Everyone else on the active roster started practice prep for Monday night’s game against the Cincinnati Bengals. That includes presumptive starting center Lucas Patrick who has been cleared from the concussion protocol and is good to go moving forward. Whether he starts or Nick Allegretti does remains to be seen, but having another solid lineman in the mix will be key.

Puka Nacua suspended 3 games for violating NFL’s personal conduct policy – SB Nation

Los Angeles Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua has been suspended for three games for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy. Last spring, Nacua faced a civil lawsuit from a woman in Los Angeles, alleging the wide receiver made an “unprovoked antisemitic statement” and later bit her on the shoulder. The lawsuit cited gender violence, assault and battery, and negligence. According to the civil lawsuit, the events in question allegedly occurred on New Year’s Eve in Century City, and it was claimed that Nacua “forcibly” bit the plaintiff on her shoulder — “leaving a circular imprint of his teeth on her body” — and that Nacua also bit the thumb of plaintiff’s friend “with such force that her companion screamed in acute pain.” The lawsuit also alleged that Nacua said “f— all the Jews,” and that the plaintiff “immediately felt uncomfortable and emotionally distressed” because of her Jewish faith.

item.title: Patriots rookie class has shown flashes so far, but questions remain
item.description: From Caleb Lomu and Gabe Jacas to the UDFAs, a look at how the Patriots’ rookies have performed so far.
item.content:encoded:
There are multiple reasons why the New England Patriots’ 2026 season so far has been one of ups and downs. Be it injuries, individual mistakes, coaching or a more challenging schedule, the team of head coach Mike Vrabel has had a tougher time playing winning football than it did a year ago.

One other factor contributing to this is the impact of the rookie class. Whereas last year’s group produced three instant starters as well as other valuable contributors, the latest batch of first-year players has not changed the team on quite the same level. Even though this means that questions do remain about the group as a whole, there have been some encouraging stretches of play as well as glimpses into a bright football.

So, with no football being played at One Patriot Place this week, let’s take a look at the that rookie class to see where its members stand 10 weeks into their professional careers.

Draft picks

OT Caleb Lomu: The Patriots traded up in the first round of the draft to select Lomu as a future starter along their offensive line. However, with Will Campbell and Morgan Moses both entrenched into the top spots at left and right tackle, respectively, the Utah product has had to start his career primarily as a backup. He has seen his most consistent action as an eligible extra blocker but did get opportunities to replace both Campbell and Moses either late in blowouts or as an injury stand-in. In total, he has played 163 snaps between left and right tackle and generally looked good. The plan therefore seemingly remains in place: he is expected to take over as New England’s right tackle as soon as this coming offseason. | 10 games (2 starts), 31.4% offensive snaps, 14.7% special teams snaps

ED Gabe Jacas: “Patience” was the theme of the offseason for New England’s second-round draft pick, who, like Caleb Lomu, was also acquired following a trade up the board. Injury recovery and contract negotiations dragged on into training camp, and when he finally took the field, Jacas did not look ready to compete. However, something started to click after the end of training camp and the start of the regular season. Since then, he has played with his hair on fire and looked like one of the best rookie edges — and one of the best defenders, period — in the class. In 10 games so far, he registered 28 quarterback pressures, including 3.5 sacks, and an interception, and leads all first-year players at his position with 14 run stops. The future is looking bright. | 10 games (0 starts), 55.5% defensive snaps, 32.0% special teams snaps

TE Eli Raridon: New England had been looking for a suitable second all-around tight end for years, and it finally seems to have found one. While Raridon’s run blocking remains a work in progress and he has been at the point of attack at multiple stuffed runs throughout the season, he has shown some promise in that area. More than that, however, he has shown promise as a pass catcher: in his nine games so far, the third-round pick caught 17 passes for 231 yards and a pair of touchdowns. The numbers are not eye-opening, but they and his 51.6% playing time share illustrate that he has been actively involved as a No. 2 tight end alongside starter Hunter Henry. It will be interesting to see if the rate of two-tight end sets featuring the pair will increase from its 16.8% over the first 10 weeks, and how Raridon’s role as a whole will develop. | 9 games (5 starts), 51.6% offensive snaps, 3.0% special teams snaps

CB Karon Prunty: Chosen in the fifth round, Prunty was the highest-picked of the Patriots’ non-roster-lock selections in this year’s draft. Despite his status as a Day 3 pick, he did manage to make the team and carve out a role as a part-time special teamer and emergency backup at cornerback. While a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury disrupted his first half-season, Prunty has developed into a Core 4 special teamer. He also has seen the field on occasion as a perimeter cornerback, even though he remains the fifth option on the positional depth chart. | 5 games (0 starts), 4.9% defensive snaps, 34.2% special teams snaps

Join the conversation!

Sign up for a user account and get:

  • Fewer ads
  • Create community posts
  • Comment on articles, community posts
  • Rec comments, community posts
  • New, improved notifications system!

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

OT Dametrious Crownover: Crownover looks like a prototypical offensive tackle, but so far he has not been given any opportunities to showcase himself at his listed position. Primarily a healthy scratch for much of the year, he played only two games so far and saw no offensive snaps. His seven combined snaps in Weeks 1 and 8 came as part of the field goal and extra point protection units. The sixth-round selection enters the bye as New England’s fifth tackle. | 2 games (0 starts), 2.6% special teams snaps

LB Namdi Obiazor: Although his defensive opportunities have been limited to late-game duty and he remains an emergency backup at his listed position, Obiazor has been actively and consistently involved so far: the sixth-rounder is ranked first on the Patriots with 223 special teams snaps and is tied for third with seven tackles. He is a Core 4 performer in the game’s third phase and has been since the start of the season. As far as late-round picks are concerned, he is performing well. | 10 games (0 starts), 4.3% defensive snaps, 83.8% special teams snaps

QB Behren Morton: With Drake Maye set to miss some time due to the ankle injury he suffered in Week 10, Morton is projected to climb up a spot on the depth chart; unless an outside free agent is brought in, he will be New England’s QB2 behind Tommy DeVito moving forward. While it remains to be seen how, if at all, that will impact his actual game-day usage, the door is now open for him to actual see the field. Previously, he served as a healthy scratch for all 10 games and only dressed because he served as the third emergency quarterback. | 0 games

ED Quintayvious Hutchins (IR): Before being placed on injured reserve with a knee injury in September, the seventh-round selection saw action in two games as a three-unit special teamer and backup edge. As such, he did not get any regular snaps outside the kicking game, playing all 16 of his defensive snaps in a lopsided Week 2 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. He did register three tackles and a quarterback hurry, though. | 2 games (0 starts), 2.5% defensive snaps, 4.5% special teams snaps

In addition to those eight players, the Patriots also selected a ninth in the draft. However, seventh-round running back Jam Miller was released ahead of roster cutdowns in late August and not brought back via the practice squad. He has been a member of the Atlanta Falcons’ practice squad since early October, but has not appeared in any games since.

Undrafted free agents

RB Myles Montgomery (IR): Despite receiving the most guarantees ever by a Patriots UDFA, Montgomery was an afterthought early in training camp. And then, on the eve of the preseason opener, he was released with an injury designation. He went unclaimed, reverted to injured reserve, and has been there ever since. | o games

WR Kyle Dixon (PS): Dixon spent his rookie training camp as a reserve wide receiver, and like the other backups at the position never made a realistic push for the active roster. His release in late August was therefore no surprise, and neither was his return via the practice squad. After all, the Culver-Stockton product had caught a team-leading 10 passes in preseason. | o games

TE Tanner Arkin (PS): Arkin wasn’t able to sustain his hot start in training camp, but he still managed to do enough to make the Patriots’ initial 53-man roster as one of three tight ends. Primarily a blocker at the position, he ended up moving between the game day roster and inactives list over the first 10 games of the season. However, an underwhelming outing against the Green Bay Packers in Week 9 likely contributed to his release the very next day. However, the team has since brought him back via the practice squad. | 5 games (2 starts), 9.3% offensive snaps, 15.4% special teams snaps

ED Xavier Holmes (PS): Holmes didn’t join the Patriots until after a successful workout as a rookie minicamp invitee, but he did have some encouraging moments in training camp. Ultimately, however, those were not enough to help him secure a spot on the team or the initial practice squad. He was brought back in mid-September and has been on the practice squad since then. | o games

LB Khalil Jacobs (IR): Together with Tanner Arkin, Jacobs was the most actively-involved undrafted rookie at this year’s training camp and like the tight end managed to survive roster cutdown day. However, he lasted only one day on New England’s 53-man roster: he was placed on injured reserve after cutdowns and despite being eligible to has not returned to practice. | o games

CB Channing Canada: Perhaps the biggest surprise of the Patriots’ 53-man team, Canada was included after seeing a steady increase in opportunities over the summer. He spent the early portions of the regular season as emergency depth before missing time due to a hamstring ailment. While seeing snaps over rookie Karon Prunty earlier in the year, the two appear to have since swapped places on the depth chart. In total, Canada has played 17 defensive snaps to Prunty’s 31 while also seeing somewhat irregular special teams work on up to five units. | 5 games (0 starts), 2.7% defensive snaps, 26.7% special teams snaps

Late additions

LB Erick Hunter: Originally signed by the Detroit Lions after going undrafted out of Morgan State, Hunter joined the Patriots shortly after his release on cutdown day. He has since served as a regular on special teams, being a part of the Core 4 return and coverage units — including, somewhat surprisingly, as a gunner on the punt team — and ranking sixth on the team in kicking game snaps (154) and tying fellow linebacker Darius Muasau for the team lead in tackles (10). His defensive contributions have been limited, but his special teams impact has been notable. | 9 games (0 starts), 3.3% defensive snaps, 57.9% special teams snaps

CB Al’zillion Hamilton (PS): Hamilton entered the NFL as rookie free agent with the Los Angeles Rams, but after spending time in training camp on the physically unable to perform list was let go in late August. He remained unsigned until early October, when the Patriots added him to their practice squad as a developmental depth option. | o games

item.title: Sam Hartman reveals why he’s doing ‘The Bachelor’ after NFL backlash
item.description: Everyone’s shocked that Sam Hartman will be the next Bachelor – including those within the Commanders organization.
item.content:encoded:
Everyone’s shocked that Sam Hartman will be the next Bachelor – including those within the Commanders organization. 

Hartman, a member of Washington’s practice squad after a long college career at Wake Forest and Notre Dame, was announced as the next star of the reality TV series where he hopes to find love despite having never seen the show before.

“I haven’t seen an episode,” Hartman revealed Thursday. “So if you guys have any tips, I would love to hear your thoughts on the do’s and do nots. But I’m gonna probably do some tape watching after the season’s over and get a study up, get the TV remote going, kind of break it down — go from the first down, the second down, third down and finally end at the Fantasy Suites.”

Hartman, who played college football from 2018-23, has not played in an NFL regular-season game, and says he’s ready to tackle the show once this season is over.

“I think playing quarterback for as long as I’ve played at the levels that I’ve played at — Notre Dame, Wake Forest — you face a lot of criticism, face a lot of praise,” Hartman said of the challenges that he will face as the star of this upcoming season, slated to begin in March. “I think it’s exciting, like you said, to showcase who I am on TV and hopefully find my teammate for life.”

Some former players, though, have questioned whether Hartman should be doing this.

Former Patriots stars Julian Edelman and Rob Gronkowski took issue with Hartman promoting the show in the middle of the season.

While former NFL tight end Clay Harbor thought it was irresponsible for Hartman to be billed as an NFL player.

“When you present yourself as an NFL player and you’ve never taken an NFL snap in an NFL football game, I take it a little bit of exception,” Harbor, who played nine seasons for the Eagles, Jaguars and Lions, said on The Score in Chicago.

“That’s a little bit of false advertisement. Am I an entrepreneur because I ran a lemonade stand in my driveway for a day? No, if you didn’t play in the NFL that’s fine, but I don’t like how you try to use it as this big springboard to make yourself sound like something you’re not… Did you do anything except get your shoulder pads measured? If you didn’t play in an NFL game, I am sorry this guy hasn’t taken an NFL snap…. It’s an accomplishment to be on a practice squad, it’s an accomplishment to play in a preseason game but you’re selling something that isn’t true. As a guy that did play over 100 games for nine years, I do think it’s like saying you’re a Navy SEAL when you passed a swimming test.”

Filming is expected to begin in January, and some of his teammates are excited to watch him. 

“It’s awesome. It’s not a distraction, first and foremost,” offensive lineman Sam Cosmi, who revealed he’s already a fan of the show. “We’re rooting for the guy, we’re rooting for Sam.”

“I had a group of guys at O-line house (in college),” Cosmi added. “We used to watch ‘The Bachelorette.’ O-linemen, we’d bring wide receivers; we had my girl and the volleyball girls come over. We had a whole thing. We watched ‘The Bachelorette,’ and it was just our thing. We had a great time with it.”

Head coach Dan Quinn added that Hartman had a nervous conversation with his practice squad quarterback. 

“When a player comes in like, ‘Hey, can I visit with you for a moment?’ You’re like, ‘Oh man, here we go … What’s going on?’” Quinn told NBC’s Cris Collinsworth. “And so I said, ‘That’s it?’ And he said, ‘Yeah,’ you know, but he was nervous. And I said, ‘I think it’s awesome, man.’”

Quinn added that Hartman is a genuinely “good dude” and added a story about why he’s the perfect candidate for the show. 

“We were playing out at the Niners on a Monday night game. We practiced over at Stanford. The coach there is Tavita Pritchard, who was our quarterback coach here. I hear his daughter running out, who’s like 4 years old: ‘Sam!’” Quinn revealed. “He made such an impact on them going to dinner at their house. And so that’s like the sign of a great teammate.”

Hartman, 27, is single and ready to mingle, though his dating life has been mostly private, and he has never married. 

He’s reportedly dated Tyla Ochoa, a former Wake Forest women’s soccer player, though it appears they broke up within the last few years.

In 2025, offensive coordinator Kliff Kingsbury said he would not let any of the Commanders’ quarterbacks “marry his hypothetical daughter” — except Hartman.

item.title: The Texans’ path to the AFC playoffs
item.description: The Texans are chasing one of two potential playoff spots right now. Here is their path.
item.content:encoded:
The Houston Texans won on Thursday night, leaping three spots in the AFC playoff picture in the process. That can go away in relatively short order, but with the schedule in front of them and the teams ahead of them, I don’t think it’s crazy to think they can go on a run.

So let’s break down the current AFC standings and check out some paths to the postseason.

AFC playoff standings with Texans win on Thursday Night Football

1. Buffalo Bills (8-1)

2. Kansas City Chiefs (7-2, 3-1 AFCW, 6-1 AFC)

3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2, 6-2 AFC, win over CIN)

4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-2, 5-2 AFC, loss to JAX)

5. Denver Broncos (7-2, 2-1 AFCW)

6. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3)

7. Cleveland Browns (6-4)

8. New England Patriots (5-5)

9. Houston Texans (4-6, 4-4 AFC, SOV tiebreaker over LV)

10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-6, 3-3 AFC)

11. Baltimore Ravens (4-6, 2-5 AFC)

12. Indianapolis Colts (3-7)

13. New York Jets (2-8)

14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .400 SOV)

15. Miami Dolphins (1-8, 1-5 AFC, .200 SOV)

16. Tennessee Titans (1-8, 1-6 AFC)

Explaining the 4-6 tiebreaker

The Texans, Raiders, and Ravens go into a three-way tiebreaker where the Ravens are eliminated on AFC record. The Texans and Texans are both .500 in that tiebreaker so it goes to Strength of Victory. The Texans’ wins came against teams with a combined 12 wins while the Raiders wins were against teams with a combined 7 wins. The Texans slip in front for now as the 9 seed. 

The Ravens and Raiders go into another tiebreaker with the Ravens’ 3-3 record in the AFC beating Baltimore’s 2-5 conference record. The Raiders are 10th. 

Explaining the 7-2 tiebreaker

The Chiefs and Broncos first go to a divisional tiebreaker, where Kansas City wins with a 3-1 record in the AFC West over the Broncos at 2-1. Kansas City is the division leader. 

The Chiefs, Jaguars, and Bengals go into a three-way tiebreaker and one team hasn’t beaten both of the others, so it moves to the AFC record tiebreaker. Kansas City wins with a 6-1 AFC record to secure the two seed for now. 

Then the Jaguars have a head-to-head win over Cincinnati to nab the three seed. 

The Broncos slot in as the top Wild Card.

The Texans’ path to the postseason

Right now, Houston is two games AND a tiebreaker behind the Cleveland Browns in the AFC and 2.5 games behind the Steelers in the six slot. The New England Patriots are in between, but they don’t have Drake Maye for this stretch run.

In the event the Steelers, Browns, and Texans are all tied, Pittsburgh and Cleveland would head to their tiebreaker first. Right now that favors Pittsburgh, which is good news for the Texans since Houston can still beat the Steelers but lost to the Browns.

If Houston beats the team on their schedule they “should” beat, they can get to 8-6 with games against the Steelers, Jaguars, and Packers determining their fate. A win over the Steelers set their floor at 9 wins and secures that tiebreaker we discussed. Then you need the Browns or Steelers to lose several games.

If both the Raiders and Texans run the table, the Raiders would move ahead in the conference record tiebreaker, so I am including them below even though they are behind Houston right now.

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 11 lineup advice
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone breaks down the Week 11 slate and provides his top lineup tips.
item.content:encoded:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench. 

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 11 rankings. 

Starts

Dak Prescott, QB, Cowboys

vs. Titans

Prescott is coming off a five-touchdown performance and a QB1 overall finish (tied with Patrick Mahomes) in Week 10. It was his fourth consecutive game with multiple scores and his second straight with over 330 passing yards. 

Another big stat line is on the way against a Titans team that went from bad to worse after trading away two of its best players, Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker. In its last two outings, Tennessee has given up 462 yards and five touchdowns to Joe Burrow in Week 8 and 352 yards and three TDs to Trevor Lawrence last Sunday.

The Cowboys are also projected for the most points of the week at 31.5. That's partially due to the elevated play volume between these two clubs. The Titans and Cowboys are first and second in neutral pace of play, setting up a busy day for both offenses. 

Other QBs to start:

  • Bo Nix vs. Raiders – Prior to the Broncos' Week 10 bye, Nix quietly finished as a fantasy QB1 in three straight contests. Now, he'll take on a Raiders defense that's the fourth-easiest matchup for passers, allowing at least two touchdown passes to each of the last eight passers they've faced.

  • Cam Ward at Cowboys – Ward will be on the other side of the high-volume affair between the Cowboys-Titans, battling a Dallas defense that's the third-most generous to quarterbacks. With Ward stating that he feels comfortable in no-huddle, the team is now using it at one of the highest rates in the league. The results speak for themselves, with Ward posting his two best fantasy outings of the season recently, finishing as the QB4 and QB12. 

Jonah Coleman, RB, Broncos

vs. Raiders

Coleman's playing time and rush share have increased in every contest during his impressive rookie campaign. 

Since returning from injured reserve, he has played 49% of the snaps and handled 50% of the carries against the Cardinals, 66% of the snaps and 61% of the carries versus the Chiefs and season-highs with 77% of the snaps and 81% of the runs in a win over the Panthers prior to Denver's Week 10 bye. 

Next up is a Raiders defense that's allowing the fifth-most fantasy points to RBs, the second-most rushing yards and the fourth-most rushing touchdowns.  

With the Broncos entering the game as 10.5-point favorites, there should be plenty of positive game script for Coleman to rack up stats en route to a fantasy RB1 finish. 

Other RBs to start:

  • Tony Pollard at Cowboys – Pollard has been on fire lately, posting 155 scrimmage yards and three TDs against the Browns, 137 yards and two scores versus the Bengals and 99 yards and a TD on a tough Jags' front. Now, he gets a revenge game against a Dallas defense that's giving up the most fantasy points to RBs. 

  • Breece Hall at Chargers – Hall has been solid since returning from his five-game injury absence, notching 87 yards and 108 yards, respectively, over the last two outings. In fact, Hall is averaging over 100 scrimmage yards in the four contests he's played that weren't impacted by the injury. The Chargers are allowing the 12th-most fantasy points, including double-digit points to seven different RBs in their last seven games. 

  • Omarion Hampton vs. Jets – Hampton finally came to life with his first 100-yard effort of the season in Week 10. There hasn't been much that's gone right for the Chargers this season, so I'd expect them to lean into Hampton's recent success. That should be easy to do against a Jets defense that's the eighth-friendliest opponent for fantasy RBs. 

Carnell Tate, WR, Titans

at Cowboys

Tate has missed the last two outings due to a shoulder injury, but fortunately he's on track to return for this shoutout. And as you can tell, we're starting almost everyone in the Titans-Cowboys game. 

Prior to getting hurt, the rookie saw at least seven targets in four of his last five appearances, while posting quality stat lines of 6-58-0, 9-145-0, 6-70-1 and 5-69-0. 

With Tate sidelined, Wan'Dale Robinson, Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor all posted notable stat lines with Tennessee pushing the pace on offense. But now Robinson is out for the year with an ankle injury. 

If Tate can avoid the trainer's table as well, he'll have a chance to post his best fantasy day yet in an uptempo contest against a Cowboys defense permitting the fifth-most points to receivers. 

Other WRs to start:

  • Rashee Rice vs. Cardinals – Even with Josh Downs joining the mix, Rice still led Chiefs receivers in targets, yards and receptions last week. He's now delivered double-digit fantasy points in four of his last five healthy games. He remains a solid fantasy WR2 in a plus matchup with Arizona. 

  • Jaylen Waddle vs. Raiders – If you don't want to start a wideout who's only gone over 40 yards twice all season, I understand. Just know that the Broncos had the second-toughest schedule for fantasy WRs in the first nine weeks and now have the 12th-easiest moving forward. That starts with a Raiders defense giving up the seventh-most fantasy points to his position, the seventh-most receiving yards overall and the most receiving touchdowns. 

  • Ryan Flournoy vs. Titans – Flournoy has put up at least 50 yards and/or a touchdown in six straight games and finished as a top-24 fantasy WR in five of those outings. Meanwhile, the Titans are the best matchup for receivers in 2026. Even as the third pass-catcher in Dallas, Flournoy can be started in fantasy as a WR3/flex option.

Chig Okonkwo, TE, Commanders

vs. Bengals

Since Terry McLaurin's season-ending injury, Okonkwo has averaged the eighth-most targets among tight ends and turned in three games with over 50 yards in five outings. 

Okonkwo likely would have accomplished that feat last week as well, had it not been for a back injury that caused him to miss part of the contest. With Okonkwo not playing his usual snaps, backup Ben Sinnott turned in four catches, 42 yards and a touchdown. 

As long as he can stay on the field, Okonkwo is set up well this week against a Bengals defense that's the ninth-best matchup for fantasy tight ends. 

Other TEs to start:

  • Mark Andrews at Panthers – The arrival of tight end whisperer Jacoby Brissett helped Andrews to his first game over 50 yards all season. The veteran caught all eight of his targets for 82 yards against the Chargers and admitted after the game that he's been playing through a broken hand since Week 3. That puts him back in the low-end TE1/high-end TE2 conversation.  

  • Mike Gesicki at Commanders – Gesicki's lack of volume is frightening, with just one or two targets in four of his last five games. However, the Bengals have the fourth-highest implied point total on the week and we know he has a nose for the end zone after scoring six touchdowns already this season. Washington is a good matchup for tight ends and receivers, so regardless of how you categorize him, Gesicki is a streaming option. 

Sits

Bryce Young, QB, Panthers

vs. Ravens

Young's early-season surge was assisted by a soft schedule through the first six weeks. Over the last month, when the schedule became more difficult, Young has struggled more often than not, getting held to 209 passing yards and one touchdown or less in three of his last four appearances. 

That stretch has also coincided with offensive line injuries that have had a negative impact on Young and the Panthers' passing attack. 

It's difficult to trust Young in a below-average matchup with the Ravens and it's not going to get better in the coming weeks. Carolina has the second-toughest slate the rest of the way, including dates with the Buccaneers, Vikings, Steelers and Seahawks before the end of the fantasy season. 

Other QBs to sit:

  • Brock Purdy vs. Vikings – While it feels wrong to have Purdy in the sit section, the degree of difficulty will be at its highest level in Week 11. Brian Flores' defense is the worst matchup for fantasy QBs by far, allowing nearly two fewer points per game than the second-place Seahawks. Minnesota has held each of the last eight passers its faced under 14 fantasy points, including Josh Allen. 

  • Jared Goff vs. Buccaneers – Tampa's defense is allowing the fourth-fewest points to quarterbacks and Goff has struggled against them the past two seasons. Goff finished as the QB21 and QB25 in those contests while only throwing one touchdown and three interceptions. 

Saquon Barkley, RB, Eagles

vs. Steelers

Since returning from injury, Barkley has managed to salvage his fantasy stat lines with a touchdown in three straight contests. However, his efficiency has been in sharp decline with just 30 rushing yards on 13 attempts in Week 8 and 22 yards on 13 carries in Week 9. He's also only seen one target in each of those outings, so you can't bank on receiving work either. 

Taking on the Steelers won't help, since Pittsburgh is allowing the third-fewest rushing yards and fourth-fewest rushing touchdowns this season. 

It's possible the Eagles could look a little better after having a bye week to regroup, but I'm not trusting Barkley as anything more than a risky TD-dependent, low-end RB2 — even in a week with six teams on bye. 

Other RBs to sit:

  • Jordan Mason at 49ers – This isn't the right matchup to start Mason. Over the last month, Mason produces enough yardage in winning game scripts to be in consideration as a fantasy flex. However, in the two losses, he managed only 20 and 35 scoreless yards, respectively. The best path to fantasy RB production against the Niners is as a pass-catcher, which isn't Mason's area of expertise.   

  • Travis Etienne Jr. at Bears – The Saints remain committed to a three-man committee approach, which limits the fantasy potential of all their backs. Etienne has now finished as the RB22, RB36, RB29 and RB40 in his games with New Orleans. Until we see something change, he's just a risky RB3/flex. 

  • Rachaad White vs. Bengals – White wasn't very productive over the last couple weeks and even before that, his best fantasy outings relied on fluky plays. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt nearing a return, White is a low-ceiling flex option. 

Deebo Samuel Sr., WR, Vikings

vs. Vikings

Samuel has made the most of his touches this year. Despite being held to four targets or less in four of his six outings, the 30-year-old playmaker has scored at least 15 fantasy points four times thanks to rushing production, touchdowns and big plays. 

While we're never going to take away someone's best plays when projecting their value moving forward, it will be challenging for Samuel to maintain those numbers on so few touches. 

The 49ers' receiver depth chart is also getting more crowded with Keenan Allen arriving via trade and Mike Evans nearing a return. 

The Vikings are the fourth-toughest matchup for fantasy WRs, so we're bumping down the outlooks for all Niners starters in this game. That makes Samuel a risky WR3/flex this week. 

Other WRs to sit:

  • Jalen Coker vs. Ravens – Coker hasn't topped 36 yards in a single game over the last month and is fresh off a zero-catch effort on four targets versus the Saints. 

  • Tre Tucker at Broncos – Tucker continues to be hit-and-miss for fantasy. A matchup with Denver's secondary isn't a spot to chase him this week. Tucker has been held under 10 yards in two of his last three games and the Broncos kept him under 30 yards in each of their encounters last year. 

  • Germie Bernard at Eagles – Bernard hasn't been able to put up more than 30 yards in any of his games over the last month and has failed to reach the end zone during that stretch. With Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson nearing a return, Bernard may have missed his window. 

Brenton Strange, TE, Jaguars

at Giants

Strange was hot in October with at least seven targets in three consecutive appearances. Sadly, that streak came to an end after the Week 7 bye when he's only seen three targets or less per game. 

With Jacksonville's ability to control games and take their foot off the gas in the fourth quarter, Strange is a tough click for fantasy. 

If this decreased volume continues, you basically have to hope Strange can find the end zone — something he's only done twice this season.  

Other TEs to sit:

  • Pat Freiermuth at Eagles – The Steelers tight ends have had one of the easier schedules over the last two months, but that's about to change. The Eagles are the sixth-toughest opponent for fantasy tight ends, which complicates things for Freiermuth since he's only topped 35 yards twice all season. 

  • Darren Waller vs. Ravens – Waller is the ultimate boom-or-bust fantasy tight end. While he offers significant touchdown potential, the floor is zeros across the board. So, I'll let you decide if you want to start a player who has three catches or less in seven of his nine appearances this season.

item.title: Out of the Den: Nick Bosa has been here before, and Sunday is Week 3
item.description: A bear isn't itself the day it leaves the den. Nick Bosa has come back from this twice. The third time is now.
item.content:encoded:
There’s a stretch every spring when the most dangerous animal in the woods is still half asleep.

Scientists have a name for it: walking hibernation. For two to three weeks after it leaves the den, the animal is on its feet, but its body is still on winter time. It moves stiffly and slowly. It stays close to home. But it hasn’t lost an ounce of what makes it dangerous. The muscle is all still there. It just doesn’t move like it yet.

Then, all at once, the woods remember what lives there.

Nick Bosa walked back into the light in Week 9. Sunday night in Mexico City is his third game back.

He’s been here before

This is the third time Bosa has torn an ACL.

The first was Oct. 30, 2015, his senior year at St. Thomas Aquinas. Right knee. His season was over before the playoffs. His dad, John, said the family was “sick about it 24 hours a day.” Two months into rehab, Nick said something that sounds a lot like him: “I think I’ll be the same player for sure.”

He had five sacks as a freshman at Ohio State. The next year, he was the Big Ten’s Defensive Lineman of the Year.

The second was Week 2 of 2020, against the Jets. Left knee. He told Richard Sherman later that during that rehab he “felt like there was no light at the end of the tunnel.” Then he came back in 2021 with 15.5 sacks and a league-high 21 tackles for loss. Even then, he said his knee “kind of improved throughout the entire season.”

That’s the pattern. He always comes back. It just takes time.

The third winter

The third was Week 3 of last season, against Arizona. Right knee again. “These surgeries are big-time traumas, physically and mentally,” he said this summer.

Then, two games into his return, a calf injury cost him five more. So for all the noise, Bosa has played four games this season.

Read the numbers, and you can tell the ground hasn’t thawed. His pressure rate is 12.5%, the lowest of his career. His get-off, how quickly he’s moving after the snap, is 0.85 seconds. In 2024, it was 0.70.

In this building, that number is gospel. Kris Kocurek has coached the 49ers’ defensive line since 2019, and everything in his room starts at the snap. Ever since, the soundtrack of a 49ers practice has been one man and four words: GTFO. And that 0.70 in 2024 was the quickest of Bosa’s career. Fifteen hundredths of a second is about a step, and the first step is always the last thing to wake up.

Offenses still plan like the muscle never left, because it didn’t. He’s seeing a chip or a double team on 32.3% of his rushes, the most of his career. And the 49ers get pressure on 35.4% of dropbacks with Bosa on the field and 29.8% without him.

“I don’t think I’m playing my best football right now,” he said Wednesday.

A plan built for a full appetite

Here’s the part that matters for Sunday.

While Bosa was out, Raheem Morris got creative. Through Week 8, the 49ers lined up five men on the line on 43.1% of snaps, more than they had in any of Kyle Shanahan’s previous nine seasons. Those five-man looks have produced pressure 38.2% of the time, up from 31.1% last year.

Then Bosa came back, DeForest Buckner came home, and the 49ers went back to rushing four. In their first game together, the five-man front fell to 21.3%. Over the first seven games, they sent five or more on 31.5% of dropbacks. In the two games since, it’s 20.9%.

The four haven’t gotten there. Over the last four weeks, the 49ers have turned one of 31 pressures into a sack, the lowest rate in the league.

The rest of the front has spent the week in Colorado getting loose. On Tuesday, six defensive linemen, Buckner included, went fly fishing on the Arkansas River. Their guide summed it up: “The fish don’t care who you are.”

Neither does Kirk Cousins. He gets sacked on just 11.1% of his pressures, the second-lowest rate in football. He gets rid of it before anything with claws can get there.

And an animal on tender feet doesn’t take the long way around. Tim Ryan, who rushed the passer in this league, said on KNBR this week that he’d like to see “fewer games and more straight rushes,” fewer stunts and more one-on-ones, and to “let these dogs eat.” Give Bosa the same tackle over and over until he finds the move that wins.

John Lynch said he expects Bosa to start “impacting games starting this week in a big way.”

Walking hibernation lasts two to three weeks. Sunday is week three. And even a groggy animal can still find full speed when something gets close enough.

And November is when bears eat.

item.title: No Bull Perspective: The Importance of Riley Moss
item.description: No Bull thoughts on how important Riley Moss is to the Denver Broncos’ defense
item.content:encoded:
I’m honestly surprised at how many comments I’ve seen since Riley Moss’ extension that are casting shade on Moss, the extension, or Moss’ play.

I think the biggest obstacle to understanding this extension and player comes from how hard it is to understand the role of cornerbacks in the NFL. So let’s start there.

Cornerback differences

There is a lot of variance you can have in the cornerback position. Are they boundary corners or nickel corners? Do they play man-to-man or zone primarily? Are they better playing off or press?

Each of these things is a big deal in how a player fits in an NFL defense.

I’m not going to break down each nuance, but let’s talk about what Riley Moss is from this set of questions.

Moss is a boundary corner. He plays on the outside of the defensive backfield, typically either manned up on a receiver or dropping into a deep zone if the call is cover-3 or quarters.

Moss excels at playing man-to-man coverage. He has no problems handling zone coverage when asked to, though.

Moss can use either technique, but is excellent at press man. This last piece is what makes him so important to the defense that Vance Joseph calls.

Why Moss helps make the defense hum

It isn’t just that Riley Moss is a better-quality player than Kris Abrams-Drane or Jahdae Barron. It is that he has no limitations on the outside. Joseph can do anything he wants with his defense when he has All-Pro Patrick Surtain II on one side and Riley Moss on the other.

Joseph can call cover-0 (requiring man coverage across the table while he blitzes from wherever he wants). He can run their typical match zone coverages. He can give safety help to a tough tight end assignment that Ja’Quan McMillian or another defensive back has. He can ask Moss to fall back into cover-3 and know Riley will handle that side of the field deep with no issues.

Defensive limitations

If you look back over the last game against Carolina, the pass defense looked pretty suspect. Moss could only play 17 snaps into the game, leaving with an injury in the middle of the 2nd quarter. Kris Abrams-Drane was out as well. That left Barron filling in with two depth safeties on the back end as well.

It’s hard to tell given the television angles, but the Broncos’ defense after Moss left was VERY different than what we’re used to seeing on the field.

They ran a lot of zone coverages throughout the game (wisely). There were too many players on the field who do not have the skill sets to play the normal aggressive press and match coverages that Joseph likes to mix in.

Heck, one of the big plays happened in the deep right zone that Surtain had and he was a solid step late getting there.

Just having Moss out there at least would have let them man the outside and let the safeties support the middle of the field.

Final Thoughts

This team is so blessed to have the three starting cornerbacks they have today. This is the most stacked the team has been at corner since the No Fly Zone.

Riley Moss is a huge part of how the defense can play aggressive mix-and-match schemes to keep offenses guessing. The flexibility we have in coverage is what has made this defense hum in the past couple of years, and it is going to be the key to how successful it is in the back half of the season.

Congratulations, Riley. You hopefully don’t pay much attention to the peanut gallery, but know that there are many of us out here who appreciate what you mean to this defense and locker room.

item.title: Should the NY Giants be interested in safety Justin Reid?
item.description: Could Justin Reid be the impact player the Giants have been looking for?
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints are expected to release veteran safety Justin Reid, per reports from Jordan Shultz and others.

It’s being reported that Reid requested to be released and is expected to sign with a playoff contender amid a messy season for the Saints. Reid, 29, is in his ninth season after being drafted by Houston out of Stanford in the 3rd round of the 2018 NFL Draft.

The Giants are in a much better place than expected at the safety position. Jevon Holland is among the best safeties in the NFL at the moment, playing elite coverage as well as being a reliable tackler coming downhill — not to mention being tied for the league lead in turnovers with six (four interceptions, two forced fumbles).

The Giants’ other safety spot has been in constant flux, with Tyler Nubin, Jason Pinnock, and Ar’Darius Washington all seeing time along with Holland. The Giants are among the NFL leaders in sub-package usage, using various defensive sub-packages on 73% of plays (T-7th), and are 5th in heavy box rate (31.1 percent).

“I think Ar’Darius played his best game the last outing against Washington,” defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson said when asked about S Ar’Darius Washington on Thursday. “Obviously, he tackled extremely well. You saw him, in the fourth quarter in a critical situation, come up with an interception. He’s been doing everything that I know he could do, from being around him in Baltimore when he was there. He is a smaller guy that plays with a big stick. He is going to attack the line of scrimmage. He tackles well. He can cover. So he’s doing a good job. I think all the safeties are doing a good job in their role. It’s kind of safety by committee. All of them deserve the opportunity to play.”

It’s worth noting that there is a connection between Reid and the Giants. He was coached by secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator Donald D’Alesio as a member of the Kansas City Chiefs from 2022 to 2024. Reid’s 2024 season was among the best of his career and the two won Super Bowls together in 2022 and 2023.

The Giants scoured the NFL for an impact player at the trade deadline, but came up empty. They currently have $7.2 million and could be interested in adding a versatile veteran safety who has played well on championship teams.

item.title: If Saints win/lose vs. Bears
item.description: What either outcome could mean for New Orleans Saints.
item.content:encoded:
The New Orleans Saints are on the road again when they face the Chicago Bears in Week 11 on Sunday. Here’s what either result could mean for the black and gold.

If the Saints win:

A win would be one of the shocks of the week across the NFL. Odds makers give the Saints little chance; they’re coming off a home game in which they blew a huge opportunity to somewhat grab a hold of the division.

Despite returning closer to full health at key positions, Kellen Moore’s squad continues to squander chances to win games.

In Chicago, there will be no room for error. If the Saints can pull it off, it drags them straight back into the playoff picture and would certainly mark a statement victory.

If the Saints lose:

A defeat to Chicago wouldn’t come as a surprise to many, and it would be another step toward missing the playoffs in the weak NFC South.

It feels as though New Orleans doesn’t have to be where they are. But even if they were nearer or above .500 right now, this is still a game that would be chalked up as a loss in a lot of fans’ eyes.

Should the Saints continue to drift away from the division lead, it won’t be the Bears game that got them there, but the ones that have come before.

Do you give the Saints a chance to pull it off in Chicago? Let us know in the comments!
